The test, at about 2:20 p.m. ET, lasted less than a minute and ran across radio, broadcast, cable and satellite TV — but not phones. By law FEMA must test the system every three years; the timing, days after a week of tech outages, was coincidental but struck some as inopportune.
articles.body: The Trump administration conducted a routine nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System on Tuesday, and officials say it went smoothly, CNN reports. The test took place at about 2:20 p.m. Eastern time, lasted less than a minute, and was broadcast across radio, broadcast, cable and satellite TV — though not on phones. 'This is a nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System, issued by the Federal Emergency Management Agency,' the message said. 'This is only a test. No action is required by the public.' By law, FEMA must test the system every three years; the last nationwide test was in October 2023, and this year's was deliberately scheduled for November so it would fall after the midterm election season. The timing was coincidental but awkward: it came days after a week of tech outages that rattled Americans about the fragility of the systems they depend on, from Microsoft to the FAA to the banks. FEMA acknowledged the noise in a post on X on Monday: 'We've heard a lot of rumors about tomorrow's EAS test. No blackouts, no secret emergencies. Just our legally mandated, routine test.' By 2:21 p.m., every channel was back to regular programming.

articles.title: Three children ended up among the famed Inca 'ice mummies' — their final moments are coming to light
articles.description: New research published in 2026 is revealing the final moments of three children — aged 6, 8 and 14 — who were sacrificed in Inca capacocha rituals some 500 years ago and preserved as 'ice mummies' on Andean summits. Medical scans and chemical analysis of hair and nails show the children were given drugs in the months and weeks before they died, and undertook monthslong journeys to peaks above 20,000 feet.
articles.body: New research published over the course of 2026 is revealing the final moments of three children — aged 6, 8 and 14 — who were sacrificed in Inca capacocha rituals some 500 years ago and preserved as 'ice mummies' on Andean summits, CNN reports. The children undertook an arduous, perhaps monthslong journey to the roughly 20,600-foot summit of Mount Ampato, a sacred Inca site high in the Andes — and they did not make it back down, not because of the climb but because they were killed as human sacrifices. Their bodies, mostly discovered in the 1990s in what is now Peru, Chile and Argentina, were so immaculately preserved by the cold, dry, high-altitude conditions that they looked asleep. New work, including medical scans and forensic and chemical analysis of hair and nail samples, is adding detail to their stories: toxicological analysis led by archaeologist Dagmara Socha of the University of Warsaw, published this month in the journal Antiquity, confirmed the children were plied with a variety of drugs in the months to weeks before they died — possibly to ease the ordeal ahead. Other research published in July in Science Advances revisited three mummies from two sacrificial sites. The children were intermediaries between the living and the divine in Inca belief, and the new science is giving them back something of their individual stories — the long journeys, the drugs, the final days — five centuries after they died.

articles.title: Why tech bros are desperate to bring Jensen Huang back — and why that would be a mistake
articles.description: Silicon Valley wants Jensen Huang back at Nvidia. The ousted chief executive thanked supporters on Tuesday, apologised for 'serious mistakes' and said he would return as CEO if the board asked — which it has not, and reportedly has no plans to do. Around 200,000 people have signed a #standwithjensen open letter, while CNN's analysis argues his return would be a mistake given the scandals that forced him out.
articles.body: Silicon Valley wants its moneymaker-in-chief back. Jensen Huang, forced to resign from Nvidia last week amid multiple scandals, has found a groundswell of support for his unlikely return, CNN reports. On Tuesday Huang thanked his supporters in a statement, apologised for 'serious mistakes' and said he would return as CEO if the board asked him — which it has not, and reportedly has no plans to do. Around 200,000 signatories of a #standwithjensen open letter have argued Huang deserves to come back, at least while an independent investigation continues. But CNN's analysis argues that bringing him back would be a mistake: his actions punctured the myth of his singular and irreplaceable leadership, and surfaced significant doubts about the viability of the company's long-term strategy. Nvidia last quarter listed $164.5 billion in land and power guarantees and AI cloud infrastructure agreements, including $20 billion in leases for data centres that have not broken ground, and the company has been accused of circular financing — funding other companies that then buy Nvidia products. One UBS analyst estimated Huang's ouster could take $50 billion out of that circular financing system. The board on Tuesday established a new national security and export control oversight committee, and the Commerce Department on Monday proposed tightened restrictions on high-end AI chip sales to Singapore. Interim CEO Colette Kress, the chief financial officer, is now running the company.

articles.title: Trump in the Philippines: Quad meeting, Thailand trade deal and ASEAN gala cap the first stop of his Asia trip
articles.description: President Trump arrived in the Philippines on Tuesday for the first stop of a three-day Asia trip, meeting Quad leaders from Australia, India and Japan for the first time since returning to the White House. He signed a trade statement with Thailand — which he said would buy $2.6 billion in US farm products — and was feted as guest of honour at the ASEAN summit gala. On Wednesday he gets full military honours from President Marcos Jr. before heading to Shenzhen for the three-way summit with Xi and Putin.
articles.body: President Donald Trump arrived in the Philippines on Tuesday, the first stop of a three-day trip that will later take him to China for historic three-way nuclear talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, CNN's morning coverage and wire reports say. After landing in Manila, Trump met with the leaders of the Quad — the US, Australia, India and Japan — for the first time since he returned to the White House last year, announcing the group would conduct an exercise featuring maritime patrol aircraft and launch an accelerator to speed the development of artificial intelligence. He signed a trade statement with Thailand, saying the country would buy $2.6 billion in US agricultural products and that he looked forward to 'finalizing the details of our formal agreement in the coming weeks'. On Tuesday night he was feted as guest of honour at the ASEAN summit gala, where leaders finalised principles to tackle online scams, according to Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. About 1,500 left-wing protesters rallied in downtown Manila ahead of his arrival, and nearly 23,000 police were deployed to secure the summit. On Wednesday Trump is set to receive a red-carpet welcome and full military honours from Marcos Jr., followed by a state banquet, and to announce commercial deals in aviation, defence, energy and technology before heading to Shenzhen for the APEC summit and the three-way meeting on Thursday.

articles.title: Tencent Music generated $1.33B in Q3, up 5.6% YoY, driven by Ximalaya acquisition, concerts, merch and Super VIP growth
articles.description: Tencent Music generated $1.33 billion in revenue in the third quarter, up 5.6% year on year, Music Business Worldwide reports. Growth was driven by the Ximalaya acquisition, concerts, merchandise and its Super VIP tier. The results cover the three months ending September 30.
articles.body: Tencent Music generated $1.33 billion in revenue in the third quarter of 2026, up 5.6% year on year, Music Business Worldwide reports. Growth was driven by the Ximalaya acquisition, concerts, merchandise and the company's Super VIP subscription tier. Tencent Music, which operates QQ Music, Kugou and Kuwo, is China's dominant music streaming company, and the Ximalaya deal — bringing the podcast and audio platform into the fold — has widened its reach beyond music into spoken audio. The results, covering the three months ending September 30, show a company still growing steadily in a Chinese market where streaming has matured and the search for new revenue has pushed platforms into live events, merch and premium tiers. Super VIP, the company's top subscription tier, continues to be a key growth engine, bundling music with perks that go beyond streaming. For the global music industry, Tencent Music's numbers are a reminder that the biggest streaming growth stories are increasingly coming from outside the West — and from businesses that treat music as one part of a broader entertainment bundle.

articles.title: Felipe Holguín named CEO of Universal Music Latin America & Iberian Peninsula
articles.description: Media and music executive Felipe Holguín has been named CEO of Universal Music Latin America & Iberian Peninsula, Music Business Worldwide reports. The entrepreneur will lead UMG's Latin operations across the region and the Iberian Peninsula. Latin music remains one of the fastest-growing segments of the global recorded music market.
articles.body: Media and music executive and entrepreneur Felipe Holguín has been named CEO of Universal Music Latin America & Iberian Peninsula, Music Business Worldwide reports. Holguín will lead UMG's Latin operations across the region and the Iberian Peninsula — a remit that covers some of the most dynamic music markets in the world. Latin music remains one of the fastest-growing segments of the global recorded music business, with streaming growth in Mexico, Brazil, Colombia and Spain consistently outpacing the global average, and Latin artists increasingly crossing over into the US and global charts. The appointment comes as the major labels compete fiercely for Latin talent and market share, with UMG, Sony and Warner all expanding their Latin divisions. Holguín's entrepreneurial background suggests UMG wants a leader who can build businesses as well as manage a catalogue — a reflection of how the Latin market rewards local partnerships, live events and artist development as much as streaming. His appointment is effective immediately, and he will be watched closely for how he positions UMG in a region where independence and local identity matter as much as global scale.

articles.title: Spotify expands Artist Profile Protection to all artists, letting them remove their name from AI fakes
articles.description: Spotify is expanding access to Artist Profile Protection, letting all artists remove their name from AI fakes and other misattributed releases on their profiles. The tool launched in beta in March. The move comes as AI-generated impersonations flood streaming services and artists struggle to police fake uploads made in their name.
articles.body: Spotify is expanding access to Artist Profile Protection, letting all artists remove their name from AI fakes and other misattributed releases appearing on their profiles, Music Business Worldwide reports. The company launched Artist Profile Protection in beta in March, and the expansion opens it to every artist on the platform. The problem it addresses is one of the most persistent complaints in the streaming era: AI-generated tracks and misattributed uploads appearing on real artists' pages, confusing fans and diluting royalties. Artists have reported fake songs uploaded under their names, sometimes racking up streams before anyone notices, and the tools to remove them have been slow and inconsistent. Spotify's move gives artists direct control over their own profiles — a meaningful shift in a system where the platform has historically decided what appears on an artist's page. It also comes as the industry's legal fight over AI training data intensifies, with labels suing Suno and other AI companies. Giving artists a practical tool to police their own identities is, for Spotify, a way to show it is acting on the problem while the courts decide the bigger questions.

articles.title: 80% of people want AI music labelled, Deezer/Ipsos survey says — as US support for AI as a musician's tool falls to 37%
articles.description: Four in five people want AI-generated music to be labelled, according to a Deezer/Ipsos survey reported by Music Business Worldwide. US respondents were 'significantly more negative' in 2026 than in 2025 on every question about AI in music — only 37% now see AI as a valuable tool for musicians, down from 54%. The findings land as the industry fights over AI training data in court.
articles.body: Four in five people want AI-generated music to be labelled, according to a Deezer/Ipsos survey reported by Music Business Worldwide — and American attitudes toward AI in music have soured sharply in a single year. Only 37% of US respondents now see AI as a 'valuable tool' for musicians, down from 54% in 2025, and Deezer said US respondents were 'significantly more negative' in 2026 than in 2025 on all questions about general attitudes to AI in music. The survey lands as the music industry's fight over AI reaches a new intensity: the major labels are suing Suno over training data, Elvis Presley's rightsholders have just added more than 100 allegedly infringing AI tracks to their suit, and Spotify has expanded tools letting artists strip their names from AI fakes. The labelling question is now one of the most concrete policy debates in music — streaming services, including Deezer itself, have begun flagging AI-generated tracks, and the survey suggests the public is firmly behind the idea. For artists and labels, the numbers are both a warning and an opportunity: audiences are open to AI as a tool, but they want to know when they are listening to it, and the industry's credibility depends on being transparent.

articles.title: Elvis Presley rightsholders amend Suno lawsuit, adding more than 100 allegedly infringing AI tracks
articles.description: Elvis Presley rightsholders have amended their lawsuit against Suno, adding more than 100 allegedly infringing AI-generated tracks. The amended filing now leads with copyright infringement and alleges Suno has created infringing output for all 859 songs in the suit. It is the latest escalation in the music industry's legal war over AI training data.
articles.body: Elvis Presley rightsholders have amended their lawsuit against Suno, adding more than 100 allegedly infringing AI-generated tracks, Music Business Worldwide reports. The amended filing now leads with copyright infringement and alleges that Suno has created infringing output for all 859 songs named in the suit — a significant expansion of the claim. The Elvis case is one of several lawsuits the music industry has brought against AI music companies, and it carries symbolic weight: Presley's voice and catalogue are among the most valuable in music, and the rightsholders are arguing that Suno's models were trained on his recordings without permission and now generate imitations of them. The amendment comes on the same day Universal and Sony fought Suno's attempt to freeze a second lawsuit, warning that the company's newest models could escape scrutiny until 2028. Together, the cases form a pincer movement: the labels are pressing in court while the rightsholders of individual iconic artists add their own claims. The central question in all of them is whether training an AI model on copyrighted recordings without a licence is infringement — and the answer will shape the economics of AI music for years.

articles.title: ElevenLabs agrees to acquire Japan-focused voice AI company Kotoba in reported $100M deal
articles.description: ElevenLabs has agreed to acquire Kotoba, a Japan-focused voice AI company, in a reported $100 million deal, Music Business Worldwide reports. Kotoba's Koto voice model already powers Japanese-language conversations in Salesforce's Agentforce Voice, and the deal is expected to close later in the fourth quarter of 2026. It is ElevenLabs' latest step in expanding beyond English-language voice AI.
articles.body: ElevenLabs has agreed to acquire Kotoba, a Japan-focused voice AI company, in a reported $100 million deal, Music Business Worldwide reports. Kotoba's Koto voice model already powers Japanese-language conversations in Salesforce's Agentforce Voice, and the deal is expected to close later in the fourth quarter of 2026. The acquisition is ElevenLabs' latest step in expanding beyond English-language voice AI and into one of the world's largest and most distinctive language markets — Japanese, with its complex honorifics and speech patterns, has been a hard problem for voice AI. ElevenLabs, which started in voice cloning and text-to-speech, has been moving aggressively into conversational AI and enterprise voice agents, and Kotoba gives it a ready-made Japanese capability plus a foothold in the Japanese market. The reported $100 million price tag is substantial for a voice AI acquisition, and it reflects how valuable high-quality, language-specific voice models have become as AI agents move into customer service, sales and entertainment. For the music industry, which watches ElevenLabs closely as a maker of AI voices, the deal is another sign that the company is building toward a global voice platform — with all the copyright and consent questions that come with it.

articles.title: Matthew McConaughey is hype for U2's Thanksgiving Eve NFL halftime show
articles.description: Matthew McConaughey is hyped for U2's Thanksgiving Eve NFL halftime show, Rolling Stone reports. The band will play the halftime show on the eve of Thanksgiving, a prime-time slot that puts them in front of one of the year's biggest TV audiences. McConaughey, a longtime U2 fan and Texas native, has been talking up the performance.
articles.body: Matthew McConaughey is hyped for U2's Thanksgiving Eve NFL halftime show, Rolling Stone reports. The band will perform at halftime of the NFL game on the eve of Thanksgiving, a prime-time slot that puts them in front of one of the biggest television audiences of the year. McConaughey, a longtime U2 fan and proud Texan, has been talking up the performance — a natural fit, given the band's deep ties to American football's biggest stages and McConaughey's own history of showing up wherever the spotlight is brightest. The show comes as U2 release their new album Carnaval De Luz, which features the collaboration with Dolly Parton, 'Torn', that just won Billboard's Favorite New Music poll. A Thanksgiving Eve halftime show is a relatively new tradition for the NFL, and U2's booking signals the league's ambition to make it a marquee event. For the band, it is another late-career stadium moment — and for McConaughey, another chance to be the most enthusiastic man in the room.

articles.title: Jason Isbell and Drive-By Truckers announce full summer tour
articles.description: Jason Isbell and Drive-By Truckers have announced a full summer tour together, Rolling Stone reports. The pairing reunites Isbell with the band he played in before going solo — a homecoming for one of Americana's biggest names. Dates and venues for the summer run were announced on Tuesday.
articles.body: Jason Isbell and Drive-By Truckers have announced a full summer tour together, Rolling Stone reports. The pairing is a homecoming: Isbell played guitar in the Drive-By Truckers from 2001 to 2007, writing songs and helping to define the band's sound on albums like Decoration Day and The Dirty South, before leaving to go solo. Since then he has become one of Americana's biggest names, winning multiple Grammys and building a devoted following for his literate, unsparing songwriting. The Truckers, meanwhile, have carried on as one of American rock's most durable institutions, releasing a steady run of albums and touring relentlessly. A joint summer tour puts Isbell back on stage with his old bandmates for a full run — the kind of reunion that fans of both acts have wanted for years. The announcement comes as Isbell continues a busy period, and as the Truckers keep up their own punishing schedule. For Americana fans, it is the summer tour to circle: two acts with a shared history, a deep catalogue between them, and a stage built for long nights.

articles.title: 'Mississippi, Lord!': Mavis Staples sings the state into a new political era
articles.description: Mavis Staples brought her gospel-soul power to the 83rd National Folk Festival, where she joined blues, gospel and roots musicians to celebrate Mississippi's musical heritage — and a historic moment of political change. Rolling Stone reports from the ground on a performance that tied the state's music to its new era.
articles.body: Mavis Staples brought her gospel-soul power to the 83rd National Folk Festival, where the soul legend joined blues, gospel and roots musicians to celebrate Mississippi's musical heritage — and a historic moment of political change, Rolling Stone reports from the ground. The festival, held in Mississippi, became a stage for a state in transition, and Staples — whose career stretches from the civil rights movement to the present day — was its natural centrepiece. Her performance tied the state's deep musical traditions to the political moment, with the report framing her set as a benediction on a Mississippi entering a new era. Staples, now in her eighties, remains one of the most commanding live performers in American music, and her presence at a folk festival celebrating the state's heritage carried a weight no younger artist could match. The piece is a reminder of how tightly music and politics are woven together in Mississippi — the birthplace of the blues, the home of gospel, and a state whose history is written in its songs. For Staples, who sang at the March on Washington and has spent six decades turning faith into music, the festival was another chapter in a career that has always been about more than entertainment.

articles.title: Priscilla Presley scores partial win over fraud suit, but claims about Lisa Marie's death can stand
articles.description: Priscilla Presley has scored a partial win in the fraud lawsuit against her, Rolling Stone reports — but the court ruled that claims about the death of her daughter, Lisa Marie Presley, can stand. The case, brought by former business partners, continues. The ruling is the latest turn in the long-running legal fight over the Presley estate.
articles.body: Priscilla Presley has scored a partial win in the fraud lawsuit brought against her by former business partners, Rolling Stone reports — but the court ruled that claims about the death of her daughter, Lisa Marie Presley, can stand. The mixed ruling keeps the case alive while narrowing parts of it, and it is the latest turn in the long-running legal fight over the Presley estate. Lisa Marie Presley died in January 2023, and the dispute over her estate — including control of Graceland and the family's business interests — has generated a series of lawsuits involving Priscilla, her granddaughter Riley Keough and former associates. The fraud suit alleges financial misconduct in dealings around the estate, and the court's decision to let the claims about Lisa Marie's death proceed means the most sensitive part of the case will be heard. Priscilla, 81, has been a central figure in the Presley estate's affairs since Elvis's death, and the litigation has played out in public for years. The partial win gives her some relief, but the case — and the family conflict behind it — is far from over.

articles.title: John Summit is extremely mad online about the Grammys
articles.description: DJ and producer John Summit is 'extremely mad online' about the Grammys after being snubbed in the 2027 nominations, Rolling Stone reports. Summit took to social media to complain that the dance and electronic categories were filled with records he considers undeserving. His rant is the latest in a long tradition of Grammy snub outrage — and a reminder of how much the nominations matter to dance artists.
articles.body: DJ and producer John Summit is extremely mad online about the Grammys after being snubbed in the 2027 nominations, Rolling Stone reports. Summit, one of the biggest names in dance music, took to social media to vent his frustration, arguing that the dance and electronic categories were filled with records that did not deserve to be there. His rant is the latest in a long tradition of Grammy snub outrage — and it lands in a year when the nominations have already generated plenty of debate, from Harry Styles being blanked entirely to BTS's absence and the surprise of Beyoncé's record 100th nomination. For dance artists, Grammy recognition has always been complicated: the genre's biggest stars often work outside the album cycle the Grammys reward, and the dance categories have long been criticised for favouring pop crossovers over club records. Summit's frustration is genuine — he is one of the most successful DJs in the world, with sold-out shows and streaming numbers to match — but it is also, as Rolling Stone's framing suggests, part of the annual ritual. Every year, someone is extremely mad online about the Grammys. This year, it is John Summit.

articles.title: Late-night hosts take aim at Trump's reaction to the FAA shutdown
articles.description: Late-night hosts have taken aim at Donald Trump's reaction to the FAA shutdown, Rolling Stone reports. The hosts mocked the president's response to the systems failure that grounded thousands of flights last week, part of a string of tech outages that has rattled the country. The jokes land as the administration tries to reassure Americans that there is no crisis.
articles.body: Late-night hosts have taken aim at Donald Trump's reaction to the FAA shutdown, Rolling Stone reports. The hosts mocked the president's response to the systems failure that grounded thousands of flights last week — part of a string of tech and infrastructure outages that has rattled the country, from a Microsoft outage to bank failures to a reported outage on the NSA's classified network. The FAA ground stop, blamed on a single newly installed router in Arkansas, stranded millions of travellers just before the weekend, and the administration's response — with Vice President JD Vance telling Fox News that 'we do not see some crisis coming down' — gave the hosts plenty of material. Late-night comedy has become one of the main ways Americans process political news, and the FAA shutdown, with its blend of high stakes and low farce, was made for it. The jokes also land at a moment when the administration is trying to reassure the public: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy has demanded as much as $50 billion in emergency funding for the FAA, and the hosts were quick to note the gap between the scale of the problem and the breeziness of the response.

articles.title: Olivia Rodrigo's album takes a fifth week at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 as Lil Baby and P1Harmony debut in the top four
articles.description: Olivia Rodrigo's you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love has taken a fifth nonconsecutive week at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, tying SOUR as her longest-running No. 1 album. Lil Baby's FRESH debuts at No. 2 with 59,000 equivalent album units, and P1Harmony's BLOW UP enters at No. 4 with 45,000 units — the K-pop group's highest chart position yet.
articles.body: Olivia Rodrigo's you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love has taken a fifth nonconsecutive week at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, tying SOUR for the longest-running No. 1 of her career, Billboard reports. The album earned 62,000 equivalent album units in the tracking week ending November 12, up 9%, according to Luminate — narrowly holding off two strong debuts. Lil Baby's FRESH enters at No. 2 with 59,000 units, his eighth top 10 album, every one of which has debuted in the top five; 55,000 of its units came from streaming, equal to 56.81 million on-demand streams. P1Harmony's BLOW UP debuts at No. 4 with 45,000 units, tying the group's highest position on the all-genre albums chart and its third top 10 album — driven by 43,500 in album sales across 25 CD variants, and topping the Top Album Sales chart for the first time. Morgan Wallen's I'm The Problem holds at No. 3 with 50,000 units. The full Billboard 200, dated November 21, is published on November 17. Rodrigo's fifth week at the top also gives her album the longest No. 1 run in 2026 for an album released this year, passing Drake's four-week stretch with ICEMAN.

articles.title: Holiday season hits the charts: Wham!'s 'Last Christmas' leads eight carols on the Hot 100
articles.description: The holiday season has arrived on the Billboard charts: Wham!'s 1984 classic 'Last Christmas' is the top-ranking holiday hit on the Hot 100, heading up eight carols on the chart. Mariah Carey's 'All I Want for Christmas Is You' — which ran up 22 weeks at No. 1 — is back in the mix, and Michael Bublé's Christmas album vaults from No. 119 to No. 35 on the Billboard 200.
articles.body: The holiday season has officially arrived on the Billboard charts, with Wham!'s 1984 classic 'Last Christmas' the top-ranking holiday hit on the Hot 100 so far, heading up eight carols on the chart. 'Last Christmas' reached a No. 2 Hot 100 high last year, just below Mariah Carey's 'All I Want for Christmas Is You', which ran up a total of 22 weeks at No. 1 — a record Ella Langley's 'Choosin' Texas' has now passed in overall weeks. The seasonal surge is visible across the charts: on the Billboard 200, Michael Bublé's Christmas album from 2011 vaults from No. 119 to No. 35, the highest-charting seasonal album of the week. Olivia Rodrigo's new holiday single, her first career Christmas song, is also making its chart debut after its November 6 release. All of Billboard's charts update each Tuesday, and the holiday takeover will only deepen in the coming weeks as streaming shifts toward seasonal listening. For the industry, the annual Christmas chart invasion is both a reliable revenue event and a reminder of how durable the catalogue is: songs recorded decades ago still dominate the most competitive weeks of the year.

articles.title: ILLIT's 'BREAK EVEN' becomes their first album to spend multiple weeks on the Billboard 200
articles.description: ILLIT's new mini album 'BREAK EVEN' has become the group's first album ever to spend more than one week on the Billboard 200, Billboard revealed on November 17. The album, which debuted at No. 6 last week, sits at No. 44 in its second week. Its title track 'You're Under Arrest' rose to a new peak of No. 22 on the Global 200.
articles.body: ILLIT's new mini album 'BREAK EVEN' has become the group's first album ever to spend more than one week on the Billboard 200, Billboard revealed on November 17. The mini album debuted at No. 6 last week — the group's first album ever to break into the top 20 — and in its second week on the chart it came in at No. 44. 'BREAK EVEN' also swept the No. 2 spots on both Billboard's Top Album Sales chart and the World Albums chart, making it the second best-selling album of the week in the United States. The group's new title track, 'You're Under Arrest', stayed strong at No. 12 on the Global Excl. U.S. chart and rose to a new peak of No. 22 on the Global 200 in its third week. ILLIT also ranked No. 58 on the Artist 100, marking their sixth overall week on the chart. For a group still early in its career, the multi-week Billboard 200 run is a meaningful milestone: debuting high is one thing, but holding on for a second week shows the album has an audience beyond its first-week fanbase. The K-pop group's steady climb continues a year in which Korean acts have been a constant presence on the American charts.

articles.title: U2 and Dolly Parton's 'Torn' wins Billboard's Favorite New Music poll
articles.description: U2 and Dolly Parton's collaboration 'Torn' has won Billboard's weekly Favorite New Music poll, taking 40% of the fan vote. The song features Parton alongside Bono and appears on U2's new album Carnaval De Luz, released November 13. It is one of Parton's final musical projects before her death on August 25, 2026, at age 80.
articles.body: U2 and Dolly Parton's collaboration 'Torn' has won Billboard's weekly Favorite New Music poll, taking 40% of the fan vote and placing ahead of the week's other new releases. The song features Parton alongside U2 frontman Bono and appears on the band's new album Carnaval De Luz, released November 13, 2026. The recording carries special significance as one of Parton's final musical projects before her death on August 25, 2026, at age 80 — a collaboration between two of the most enduring acts in popular music, recorded in the last months of her life. The poll win reflects strong support among participating fans, and it caps a week in which U2 have been everywhere: the album's release, the Thanksgiving Eve NFL halftime show announcement, and now a fan-voted chart victory. For Parton's legacy, 'Torn' is a fitting final chapter — a duet with a band she admired, on an album that pairs her voice with one of rock's biggest stages. The 40% vote share is a decisive margin in Billboard's weekly poll, and it suggests the collaboration has connected with both U2's and Parton's audiences.

articles.title: Ukraine strikes the Crimean Bridge a second time in two days, sending a road arch crashing into the sea
articles.description: Ukrainian forces struck the Crimean Bridge again overnight on November 17, the second attack in two days, and a section of the road arch collapsed into the sea, halting all road and rail traffic. President Zelenskyy called it an “unprecedented operation” and said Ukraine used Neptune and Flamingo missiles. Russia’s occupation authorities confirmed the damage while Moscow played it down.
articles.body: Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge overnight on November 17, the second strike on the crossing in two days, and monitoring channels reported that one of the road arches had fallen into the sea. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said preparations for the strikes took several weeks and described the operation as “unprecedented,” adding that the final stage involved Neptune and Flamingo missiles and that it was the seventh stage of a multi-week campaign. The SBU said the bridge’s road section was destroyed and that “no car will pass” on it, while the railway section was also damaged and shipping through the Kerch Strait was disrupted. The first strike on November 16 had halted traffic for about twelve hours before it partially resumed, and OSINT analysts said the main road span was visibly deformed even as Moscow called the damage “insignificant.” The 19-kilometre bridge is Russia’s only direct land link to occupied Crimea and a key supply route for its forces, and it has been attacked several times since 2022. Russia’s defence ministry claimed more than 1,400 Ukrainian drones attacked Russia and Crimea overnight in response.

articles.title: Russia strikes bridges over the Dnipro in Kyiv
articles.description: Russian forces struck bridges over the Dnipro river in Kyiv overnight on November 17, forcing their closure to traffic, Ukrainian authorities said. President Zelenskyy said four ballistic missiles hit the Southern Bridge and three hit the Northern Bridge. He said Ukraine needs a reserve crossing.
articles.body: Russian forces struck bridges over the Dnipro in Kyiv overnight on November 17, forcing their closure to traffic, Ukrainian authorities said. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said four ballistic missiles hit the Southern Bridge and three hit the Northern Bridge, and that Ukraine needs a reserve crossing to keep the capital connected. The strikes on the capital’s bridges came on the same night Ukraine hit the Crimean Bridge for the second time in two days, and they follow months of intensified Russian attacks on bridges inside Ukraine. Air defences reported downing three missiles and more than 200 Russian drones overnight, with impacts at 44 locations, and parts of nine regions were left without power. The bridge strikes are part of a mutual campaign against transport infrastructure: Ukraine has been hitting Russian refineries, ports and the Crimean Bridge, while Russia has been targeting Ukraine’s power grid and river crossings as winter approaches.

articles.title: More than 1,400 Ukrainian drones attacked Russia and Crimea, Russia’s Defence Ministry says
articles.description: More than 1,400 Ukrainian drones attacked Russia and Crimea overnight, Russia’s Defence Ministry said. Ukrainian drones hit industrial zones in Ufa and Salavat, in Bashkortostan, according to local emergency officials. The barrage came on the same night Ukraine struck the Crimean Bridge for the second time in two days.
articles.body: Russia’s Defence Ministry said more than 1,400 Ukrainian drones attacked Russia and Crimea overnight, in one of the largest drone barrages of the war. Ukrainian drones attacked industrial zones in Ufa and Salavat, the Bashkortostan State Committee for Emergency Situations reported, and fires were reported in Russia’s Rostov region, with an oil depot said to be burning in Azov. The scale of the claimed attack underlines how the long-range drone war has escalated on both sides: Russia launched 158 drones at Ukraine on the night of November 15-16, and Ukraine has been systematically striking Russian refineries, ports and military infrastructure. Moscow routinely claims to shoot down the vast majority of incoming drones, and the figures cannot be independently verified. The barrage coincided with Ukraine’s second strike on the Crimean Bridge in two days, which collapsed a road arch into the sea.

articles.title: Russian lawyer Maria Bontsler, 66, sentenced to 12 years in prison for ‘treason’
articles.description: A court in Kaliningrad has sentenced 66-year-old lawyer Maria Bontsler to 12 years in a penal colony for ‘treason.’ Bontsler spent her career defending abused conscripts, protesters and war critics. Her case is the latest in a wave of treason prosecutions against lawyers, journalists and activists.
articles.body: On November 12, a court in Kaliningrad sentenced 66-year-old lawyer Maria Bontsler to 12 years in a penal colony for ‘treason,’ Meduza reported. Bontsler’s career began in the 1990s, when she defended the rights of abused conscripts, protesters and critics of the war in Ukraine. Her prosecution is part of a broader crackdown in which treason and related charges have been used against lawyers, journalists, scientists and activists, with sentences that have grown steadily harsher since the full-scale invasion began. The case drew attention because of Bontsler’s age and her decades of human-rights work, and because it targets a defence lawyer — a profession that has itself become a target as the Russian state narrows the space for any legal defence of its critics. The sentence sends a message to the shrinking community of lawyers still willing to take on politically sensitive cases.

articles.title: Kallas: data on Russian soldiers ‘quite easy’ to obtain for EU entry ban; Duma speaker threatens her with 20 years
articles.description: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said the European Union is continuing to discuss a ban on entry for Russians who have fought in the war, and that obtaining their data would be “quite easy.” Russia’s State Duma speaker responded by threatening her with 20 years in prison. The exchange follows a push for entry bans on Russian veterans and athletes competing under the national flag.
articles.body: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said the European Union is continuing to discuss a ban on entry for Russians who have fought in the war in Ukraine, and that obtaining their data would be “quite easy.” Russia’s State Duma speaker responded by threatening Kallas with 20 years in prison, in the latest rhetorical escalation between Moscow and Brussels. The EU is weighing entry bans for Russians who fought in Ukraine, alongside a ban on Russian athletes competing under the national flag, as part of a broader package of measures against Moscow. Kallas has been one of the most hawkish voices in the EU on Russia, and she has also argued that the EU must seek a ceasefire before detailed talks with Russia, calling Moscow’s demands “absurd.” The spat shows how the sanctions debate has moved beyond economics into questions of personal accountability for those who took part in the invasion.

articles.title: EU sanctions Russia’s biggest oil refineries, payment service YooMoney and more than 40 banks
articles.description: The European Union has expanded its sanctions against Russia to include its biggest oil refineries, petrochemical plants, the payment service YooMoney and more than 40 banks. The bloc also sanctioned Tatyana Kim, founder of e-commerce giant Wildberries, over alleged military supply ties. It is the latest round of pressure as peace talks continue.
articles.body: The European Union has expanded its sanctions list targeting Russia to include the country’s biggest oil refineries, petrochemical plants and companies, and dozens of banks, Meduza reported. The payment service YooMoney is among those sanctioned, along with more than 40 banks. The bloc also added Tatyana Kim, the founder of Russian e-commerce giant Wildberries, to its sanctions list over alleged military supply ties, French foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot said. The measures are aimed at choking off revenue for Russia’s war effort and follow a series of Ukrainian long-range strikes on Russian energy infrastructure, including the Ust-Luga port. They come a day after the EU Council approved a nearly €8 billion payment to Ukraine, the largest single disbursement yet under the Ukraine Facility. The sanctions land as US, Russian and Ukrainian negotiators prepare for a new round of talks, with the Kremlin insisting the next round will be trilateral and without Europe.

articles.title: Nuclear regulators from 38 countries warn of a growing risk of a nuclear accident in Ukraine this winter
articles.description: Nuclear regulators from 38 countries have warned of a growing risk of a nuclear accident in Ukraine this winter and urged Russia to stop striking the power grid. The risk is rising as Russia steps up attacks on the country’s energy infrastructure, Reuters reported. Parts of nine Ukrainian regions were left without power after the latest shelling.
articles.body: The risk of a nuclear accident in Ukraine this winter is rising as Russia steps up attacks on the country’s energy infrastructure, Reuters reported, citing a warning from nuclear regulators in 38 countries. The regulators urged Russia to stop striking the power grid, which supplies cooling and safety systems to Ukraine’s nuclear power plants. The warning comes as Russian strikes have repeatedly knocked out power to parts of the country, with the latest shelling leaving parts of nine regions without electricity and emergency outage schedules introduced in three more. Ukraine’s nuclear plants have already been forced to reduce output or rely on emergency power during earlier attacks on the grid. Regulators fear that a sustained loss of off-site power during the coldest months could strain safety margins at plants that were designed to operate with a stable grid connection.

articles.title: Putin invokes a law countering ‘unfriendly’ countries to seize dead Russians’ unclaimed cash and gold
articles.description: Vladimir Putin has issued a decree establishing a process for the state to seize unclaimed cash, gold and other property left by Russians who die without heirs. The decree is titled “On certain aspects of the transfer of heirless property into the ownership of the Russian Federation.” It was issued under a law countering ‘unfriendly’ countries.
articles.body: In early November, Vladimir Putin issued a decree titled “On certain aspects of the transfer of heirless property into the ownership of the Russian Federation.” The decree establishes a process for the state to take ownership of cash, gold and other property left behind by Russians who die without heirs, and it was issued under a law framed as countering ‘unfriendly’ countries. The move is the latest in a series of measures tightening state control over private property and capital, and it comes as the Russian state looks for new sources of revenue and assets amid the costs of the war and sanctions. Critics note the irony of a state that has driven hundreds of thousands of its citizens into exile now moving to claim the property of those who die without anyone to inherit it. The decree’s practical reach is unclear, but it signals that no category of private wealth is beyond the state’s grasp.

articles.title: SBU: the Crimean Bridge’s road section is “dead” — no car will pass on it
articles.description: The Security Service of Ukraine says the Crimean Bridge’s road section is destroyed and impassable for vehicles after the overnight strike. One of the bridge’s arches fell into the sea and all traffic was stopped. Putin’s side promised to rebuild the bridge “even better” than before.
articles.body: The Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) said the Crimean Bridge’s road section is destroyed and that no car will be able to pass on it, after Ukrainian forces struck the crossing overnight on November 17. One of the bridge’s arches fell into the sea, the railway section was damaged, and all road and rail traffic was suspended. It was the second attack on the bridge in a day, after a first strike on November 16 that had halted traffic for about twelve hours. President Zelenskyy said the operation used Neptune and Flamingo missiles and was the seventh stage of a campaign prepared over several weeks. Russia’s occupation authorities confirmed the damage, while Putin’s office promised to rebuild the bridge “even better” than it was. The bridge is Russia’s only direct land link to occupied Crimea and a key supply route for its forces in the south.

articles.title: Zelenskyy: Ukraine used Neptune and Flamingo missiles on the bridge; SBU says its road section is “dead”
articles.description: President Zelenskyy said Ukraine’s defence forces used Neptune and Flamingo missiles in the overnight strike on the Crimean Bridge, describing it as the seventh stage of a weeks-long operation. The SBU said the bridge’s road section is destroyed and “no car will pass” on it. Kyiv also reported Russian strikes on bridges over the Dnipro in the capital.
articles.body: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy listed the weapons Ukraine’s defence forces used to strike the Crimean Bridge, saying the operation employed Neptune and Flamingo missiles and was the seventh stage of a campaign prepared over several weeks. The Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) said the bridge’s road section was destroyed, with one arch falling into the sea, and that no vehicle would be able to use it. Zelenskyy also said four ballistic missiles hit Kyiv’s Southern Bridge and three hit the Northern Bridge, and that a reserve crossing was needed after Russian forces struck bridges over the Dnipro in the capital overnight, forcing their closure to traffic. Ukrainian air defences reported downing three missiles and more than 200 Russian drones overnight, with hits recorded at 44 locations, and Russian drones killed two people in Kharkiv region. Parts of nine regions were left without power after shelling, with emergency outage schedules introduced in three more. Moscow, for its part, promised to rebuild the bridge “even better” than before.

articles.title: Zelenskyy: four ballistics hit the Southern Bridge, three the Northern — a reserve crossing is needed
articles.description: President Zelenskyy said four ballistic missiles hit Kyiv’s Southern Bridge and three hit the Northern Bridge in the overnight Russian attack. He said Ukraine needs a reserve crossing for the capital. Russian forces struck bridges over the Dnipro, forcing their closure to traffic.
articles.body: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said four ballistic missiles hit Kyiv’s Southern Bridge and three hit the Northern Bridge in the overnight Russian attack, and that a reserve crossing is needed for the capital. Russian forces struck bridges over the Dnipro in Kyiv overnight on November 17, forcing their closure to traffic, Ukrainian authorities said. The strikes on the capital’s bridges came as Ukraine hit the Crimean Bridge for the second time in two days, and they underline how both sides are now targeting transport infrastructure. Air defences reported downing three missiles and more than 200 Russian drones overnight, with impacts at 44 locations. The bridge attacks are part of Russia’s wider campaign against Ukrainian infrastructure as winter approaches, with power outages already affecting parts of nine regions.

articles.title: Hungary suspends rail links with Ukraine after Russian attacks
articles.description: Hungary is suspending rail links with Ukraine because of Russian attacks, according to Hungarian officials. Budapest also said a Russian strike on the Zakarpattia region is unlikely to be the last. The suspension cuts a key transport link between Ukraine and the EU.
articles.body: Hungary is suspending rail links with Ukraine because of Russian attacks, Hungarian officials said, in a move that cuts a key transport connection between Ukraine and the European Union. Budapest also said the Russian strike on the Zakarpattia region, in western Ukraine near the Hungarian border, is unlikely to be the last. The suspension is a significant step: rail has been one of the main arteries for people, aid and goods moving between Ukraine and the EU since the full-scale invasion began. Hungary’s government has been the most sceptical in the EU about support for Ukraine, and the decision will be read in Kyiv as another sign of the strains in the relationship. It also raises practical questions about alternative routes for cross-border traffic if the suspension lasts.

articles.title: Parts of nine regions without power after shelling; emergency outage schedules in three more
articles.description: Parts of nine Ukrainian regions are without power after the latest Russian shelling, with emergency outage schedules introduced in three more regions. The strikes are part of Russia’s campaign against the energy grid as winter approaches. Nuclear regulators from 38 countries have warned of a growing risk of a nuclear accident.
articles.body: Parts of nine Ukrainian regions are without power after the latest Russian shelling, with emergency outage schedules introduced in three more regions. The outages are the result of Russia’s sustained campaign against Ukraine’s energy infrastructure, which has intensified as winter approaches and temperatures fall. Nuclear regulators from 38 countries have warned of a growing risk of a nuclear accident in Ukraine this winter and urged Russia to stop striking the power grid, which supplies cooling and safety systems to the country’s nuclear plants. Ukrainian air defences reported downing three missiles and more than 200 Russian drones overnight, but impacts were recorded at 44 locations. The sixth blackout in two weeks recently left almost half of Dnipro without power, showing how the grid is being worn down strike by strike.

articles.title: Air defences down three missiles and more than 200 Russian drones overnight; two killed in Kharkiv region
articles.description: Ukrainian air defences downed three missiles and more than 200 Russian drones overnight, with hits recorded at 44 locations. Russian drones killed two people in the Kharkiv region. The barrage came on the same night Ukraine struck the Crimean Bridge for the second time in two days.
articles.body: Ukrainian air defences downed three missiles and more than 200 Russian drones overnight, according to the latest feed from Ukraїnska Pravda, with hits recorded at 44 locations despite the interceptions. Russian drones killed two people in the Kharkiv region, where an active evacuation from 96 settlements is continuing after the mandatory evacuation zone was expanded. The overnight barrage was one of the largest in recent weeks and came on the same night Ukraine struck the Crimean Bridge for the second time in two days. Russia’s General Staff reported 135 combat engagements over the past day, with the heaviest fighting on the Pokrovsk direction, where Russian forces launched two missile strikes, 90 airstrikes, used 9,018 kamikaze drones and conducted 2,284 shellings. The figures underline that neither side is easing the long-range war even as peace diplomacy intensifies.

articles.title: IMF nears a $1.6 billion staff agreement with Ukraine but cuts its GDP forecast
articles.description: The International Monetary Fund has reported significant progress in talks with Ukraine toward a staff-level agreement that could unlock about $1.6 billion in financing. At the same time, the IMF cut its GDP forecasts for Ukraine for 2026 and 2027 to negative growth, citing the worsening security situation and Russian strikes on economic infrastructure.
articles.body: The International Monetary Fund has reported significant progress in talks with Ukraine’s government toward a staff-level agreement on the combined second and third reviews of its EFF programme, which could unlock about $1.6 billion in financing. The IMF said the talks had advanced substantially, in a boost for Kyiv as it seeks to keep international funding flowing. At the same time, the Fund downgraded its GDP growth forecasts for Ukraine for 2026 and 2027 to negative territory, citing the worsening security situation and Russia’s intensified strikes on economic infrastructure. The combination of new money and a gloomier outlook captures Ukraine’s economic bind: external support is holding, but the war’s damage to infrastructure and industry is deepening. The agreement still needs to be finalised at staff level before the money can be released.

articles.title: Witkoff and Kushner to meet Ukrainian and European officials in Berlin on November 19
articles.description: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner plan to meet Ukrainian and European officials in Berlin on November 19 to discuss security guarantees for Ukraine, post-war economic recovery and the format of the next negotiating round. The meeting comes as the Kremlin says the next US-Russia-Ukraine talks will be trilateral, without Europe.
articles.body: US presidential envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner plan to meet Ukrainian and European officials in Berlin on November 19, to discuss security guarantees for Ukraine, plans for post-war economic recovery and the possible format of the next negotiating round. The Berlin meeting is part of a crowded diplomatic week: China has confirmed that Xi Jinping will host Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on the same day, and the Kremlin says the next round of US-Russia-Ukraine peace talks will be trilateral, without Europe. Kyiv has been pushing for European participation in the talks, and the Berlin session is a chance for Ukraine and its European partners to align positions before the leaders meet. The diplomacy comes as Ukraine’s negotiators are reported to be pursuing two parallel tracks on the Donbas question, with intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov and faction leader Davyd Arakhamia advancing different approaches inside the same delegation.

articles.title: Stellar Blade developers are interested in making games for Xbox — and have their eye on Project Helix
articles.description: Shift Up, the studio behind Stellar Blade, has expressed interest in making games for Xbox consoles. Technical director Lee Dong-gi said at the Console Game Developers Conference 2026 that the team is particularly interested in Xbox Project Helix. The studio hopes to be among the first to receive next-generation devkits.
articles.body: Shift Up, the Korean studio behind Stellar Blade, has expressed interest in developing games for Xbox consoles, technical director Lee Dong-gi said during a talk at the Console Game Developers Conference 2026. He said he and his colleagues are particularly interested in Xbox Project Helix, Microsoft’s next-generation console, and that the studio is ready to take advantage of what the new hardware offers. Shift Up hopes to be among the first developers to receive next-generation devkits. The studio has so far released only one console game, and is now working on Stellar Blade: Blood Rain and Project Spirits. Stellar Blade was originally planned as a multi-platform release, but after a partnership with Sony it became a temporary PlayStation 5 console exclusive; after the announcement of a Nintendo Switch 2 version, Xbox fans flooded the studio with requests for a port. The interest is a small sign of how Microsoft’s next console is already shaping developers’ plans.

articles.title: First game from Resident Evil creator Shinji Mikami’s new studio due in 2027
articles.description: The first game from Unbound Games, the new studio of Resident Evil and The Evil Within creator Shinji Mikami, is planned for release in mid- to late 2027. Mikami said it will be a “relatively small but very exciting and completely new in spirit” game. The studio was acquired by Stellar Blade maker Shift Up in March 2026.
articles.body: The first game from Unbound Games, the new studio founded by Resident Evil and The Evil Within creator Shinji Mikami, is planned for release in mid- to late 2027, Mikami said in an interview with the Japanese podcast Alco and Peace. He stressed that it will be a “relatively small but very exciting and completely new in spirit” game, and that the studio has no plans to start with a big blockbuster. The compact release will be just the first step for the new team. In March 2026 the studio was acquired by South Korean company Shift Up, the maker of Stellar Blade and Goddess of Victory: Nikke. The partnership plans to produce several projects at once, including both smaller auteur releases and full-scale AAA games. For fans of survival horror, Mikami’s return to directing a new game — rather than producing — is one of the most anticipated comebacks in the industry.

articles.title: The Game Awards 2026 nominees are revealed tonight — and GTA VI launches on Thursday
articles.description: The Game Awards 2026 nominees will be announced tonight at 20:00 Moscow time, with Geoff Keighley promising the biggest show in the ceremony’s history on December 10. The reveal comes two days before Grand Theft Auto VI launches on Thursday, November 19 — the most anticipated release of the year. The ceremony will stream on YouTube, Twitch, Disney+ and even inside Roblox.
articles.body: The nominees for The Game Awards 2026 will be announced on Tuesday, November 17, at 20:00 Moscow time, with host Geoff Keighley presenting the contenders in a special livestream on YouTube and Twitch, after which fan voting opens on the show’s website. The ceremony itself takes place on December 10 at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, with the broadcast starting at 03:30 Moscow time on December 11. Keighley says this year will be the most ambitious show in the awards’ history, and for the first time the broadcast will also run on Disney+, inside Roblox and in the Live TV app on PlayStation 5, alongside the usual streaming platforms. The announcement lands in the middle of launch week for Grand Theft Auto VI, which arrives on Thursday, November 19, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S — a release so big that much of the industry cleared its calendar around it. The week’s other releases are mostly smaller indie titles and expansions living in GTA’s shadow.

articles.title: Ubisoft greenlights a new Rainbow Six: Vegas — codename “Spades”
articles.description: Ubisoft has approved development of a new Rainbow Six: Vegas game, Insider Gaming’s Tom Henderson reports. The project, codenamed “Spades,” is in early production at Ubisoft Montreal and is expected to be a full sequel — effectively Vegas 3 — rather than a remake. An official announcement is likely years away.
articles.body: Ubisoft has approved the development of a new Rainbow Six: Vegas game, journalist Tom Henderson of Insider Gaming reported, citing his own sources. The project, codenamed “Spades,” is in early production at Ubisoft Montreal and is most likely to be called simply Rainbow Six: Vegas 3, though no details have been confirmed. It would be a full sequel rather than a remake, nearly two decades after Vegas 2 came out in 2008. Ubisoft counts Rainbow Six among its three key franchises, alongside Far Cry and Assassin’s Creed, and the Vegas revival is one of three new projects greenlit at Ubisoft Montreal, with at least one other also set in the Rainbow Six universe. The studio is also planning a tactical Rainbow Six Tactics for 2027. The development is part of a wider expansion under Vantage Studios, the subsidiary that now oversees Ubisoft’s biggest franchises, in which Tencent holds a 26.32 percent stake. Fans should not expect an official announcement for several years.

articles.title: GTA VI launches on Thursday — the release the whole industry cleared its calendar for
articles.description: Grand Theft Auto VI launches on Thursday, November 19, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. It is the most anticipated game release of the year, and much of the industry moved its own releases out of the way. The week’s other new games are mostly smaller titles launching in its shadow.
articles.body: Grand Theft Auto VI launches on Thursday, November 19, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, and it is the release the entire games industry has been waiting for. The launch is so big that other publishers spent the year moving their games out of November, and the week’s remaining releases are mostly smaller indie titles and expansions. The game arrives with a full album of new music attached — the 34-track GTA VI: The Album tracklist leaked online last week, with new songs from Lana Del Rey, Dua Lipa and Zara Larsson. The launch caps a week dominated by Rockstar: the Game Awards nominees are announced tonight, and the industry is watching whether GTA VI sweeps the nominations. It will not be available on PC at launch. For players, Thursday is the day the year’s biggest entertainment release finally arrives.

articles.title: US intelligence is concerned Iran may be plotting a dirty-bomb attack in Washington, sources say
articles.description: US intelligence is concerned Iran may be plotting to use a dirty bomb in Washington, DC, sources told CNN, though officials are divided on whether Tehran could pull it off. The White House says there is no credible threat right now. The warning lands as the administration tries to calm fears after a chaotic week of tech outages.
articles.body: US intelligence is concerned that Iran may be plotting a radiological “dirty bomb” attack in Washington, DC, sources told CNN in an exclusive report on Monday. Officials are divided on whether Tehran has the capability or the intent to carry out such an attack, and the White House says there is no credible threat at present. A dirty bomb uses conventional explosives to scatter radioactive material rather than causing a nuclear explosion, but even an unsuccessful attempt would be a major escalation. The report comes amid already heightened US-Iran tensions and as the Trump administration works to reassure the public after a string of unrelated disruptions — a Microsoft outage, an FAA systems failure and banking outages — that rattled travel, business and banking for millions of people. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said he could say with 98 percent certainty that the incidents were not a coordinated cyberattack. The administration is keen to draw a line between a genuine intelligence concern and the week’s technical failures.

articles.title: Trump lands in the Philippines for a Southeast Asian leaders’ summit
articles.description: Donald Trump has arrived in the Philippines to attend a summit of Southeast Asian leaders, as his Asia trip continues toward a closely watched three-way meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. Live coverage followed his remarks alongside Thai prime minister Anutin Charnvirakul. The trip comes days after Democrats swept the US midterms.
articles.body: President Donald Trump landed in the Philippines on Tuesday to attend a summit of Southeast Asian leaders, with CNN carrying live updates of his remarks alongside Thai prime minister Anutin Charnvirakul. The stop is part of a wider Asia trip that is building toward a planned three-way meeting with China’s Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin, which China has confirmed Xi will host in Shenzhen on November 19. The Financial Times has reported the trilateral meeting will take place without a pre-agreed agenda. The Kremlin says the next round of US-Russia-Ukraine peace talks will be trilateral, without Europe, while Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are due in Berlin on November 19 to meet Ukrainian and European officials about security guarantees for Ukraine. The diplomacy is the most active it has been in months, and it is unfolding just days after Democrats flipped both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections, with the new majorities taking their seats on January 3.

articles.title: Trump administration dismisses crisis fears after a string of disruptive tech outages
articles.description: Top Trump administration officials sought to reassure Americans and dismiss fears of a possible crisis after a string of major tech and infrastructure failures disrupted travel, business and banking. Vice President JD Vance said: “We do not see some crisis coming down.” There is no evidence the incidents were connected.
articles.body: Top officials from the Trump administration sought to reassure Americans and dismiss fears of a possible crisis after a string of major tech and infrastructure failures disrupted travel, business and banking for millions of people. “We do not see some crisis coming down. But you have to be prepared for everything,” Vice President JD Vance told Fox News in an interview released on Monday, adding that friends had asked him whether they should be building bunkers or stocking up on food and water. The chaotic week began last Thursday, when a massive Microsoft outage left people worldwide without Outlook email and Teams, which Microsoft said was caused by a “technical issue” that took roughly two days to fix at a potential cost of $7 billion. Before that was fully resolved, the FAA suffered a systems failure on Friday that cancelled thousands of flights, which the agency suspects was caused by a single newly-installed router in Arkansas. On Monday, major banks reported issues, with thousands of Chase customers unable to use online accounts; Chase said it was a software bug. United Airlines then reported a short-lived system outage that delayed fewer than 150 flights. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said he could say with 98 percent certainty the incidents were not a coordinated cyberattack. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy has demanded as much as $50 billion in emergency funding to update air traffic control systems.

articles.title: Analysis: the critical new geopolitical truth behind Trump’s defence of the former Nvidia chief
articles.description: CNN’s analysis links Donald Trump’s defence of former Nvidia chief Jensen Huang to a wider geopolitical shift around AI chips and China. The Nvidia story — which involves claims of spying, sex and corporate intrigue — has much bigger stakes than the personal drama, the network argues. The administration has also tightened AI chip export curbs ahead of Trump’s China trip.
articles.body: CNN’s analysis argues that Donald Trump’s defence of former Nvidia chief Jensen Huang points to a critical new geopolitical truth about the contest over AI chips and China. The Nvidia story, which has drawn headlines for its mix of spying, sex and corporate intrigue, is about much more than personal drama, CNN says: it is about who controls the most advanced semiconductors in the world and on what terms they can be sold to China. The administration has tightened AI chip export curbs ahead of Trump’s trip to China, where he is due to meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has become a central figure in the story, with a separate CNN analysis arguing he is “one big problem” for the administration. The Nvidia saga has become a proxy for the wider debate inside Washington about whether to contain China’s AI ambitions or to keep selling it the chips that power them.

articles.title: Forensic expert says Epstein was likely killed, but NYC medical examiner stands by suicide ruling
articles.description: A forensic expert says Jeffrey Epstein was likely killed, while New York City’s medical examiner maintains the suicide ruling. The claim revives one of the most persistent conspiracy theories in American public life. President Trump has said he would sign a bill to release the Epstein files.
articles.body: A forensic expert says Jeffrey Epstein was likely killed, while New York City’s medical examiner stands by its ruling that Epstein died by suicide, CNN reported. The claim revives one of the most persistent and politically charged questions in American public life: how the financier died in a Manhattan jail cell in 2019 while awaiting trial on sex-trafficking charges. The medical examiner has consistently maintained the death was a suicide, and no official finding has changed that conclusion. The new claim lands as pressure builds for the release of the Epstein files, with President Trump saying he would sign a bill to release them. The files have become a political football, with both parties using them to attack each other, and the latest forensic claim is likely to fuel further demands for transparency rather than settle the question.

articles.title: $100,000 pay, very little training: the data-center jobs no one knows about
articles.description: In the race to build America’s AI infrastructure, tech companies are struggling to find technicians to install cooling, server racks, electrical equipment and fibre-optic cables. Some of the jobs pay more than $100,000 a year after just two days of training. The US is short about a million engineers for data-center construction, PwC estimates.
articles.body: Two days of training end with a diploma reception, and companies eager to hire the new graduates come ready to hand out jobs that can pay more than $100,000 a year. Welcome to the data-center economy. In the race to build out America’s AI infrastructure, tech companies are struggling to find technicians with the skills to install the cooling, server racks, electrical equipment and fibre-optic cables needed to meet off-the-charts demand. Several nonprofits, online learning companies and all four of the big AI hyperscalers — Amazon, Google, Meta and Microsoft — offer free, accelerated training courses for the technical skills needed to build data centres. AI infrastructure spending is expected to approach $1 trillion a year for the foreseeable future, according to Columbia Business School economist Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh. The United States has a shortage of one million engineers needed to meet data-center construction estimates, PwC estimates, and only about half of the AI computing capacity scheduled to come online between now and 2028 is expected to meet its target date, according to Goldman Sachs. For large AI data centres, a month of delay can cost anywhere from tens of millions to well over $100 million.

articles.title: Democrats hope a familiar name can help put Indiana back in play
articles.description: Democrats are dreaming of building on their midterm gains across Middle America, and in Indiana a scion of the state’s most famous political family is igniting hopes that the Rust Belt’s reddest state might soon be in play. Beau Bayh, 31, grandson of Senator Birch Bayh and son of former governor Evan Bayh, won the secretary of state’s race in his first run for office, improving by 28 points on Trump’s 2024 margin.
articles.body: Democrats are dreaming of building on their midterm gains across Middle America, and in Indiana, a scion of the state’s most famous political family is igniting the party’s hopes that the Rust Belt’s reddest state might soon be in play. Beau Bayh, the 31-year-old grandson of Senator Birch Bayh and son of Evan Bayh, the former governor and senator, did not just win the Indiana secretary of state’s race in his first run for political office. He was perhaps the party’s single strongest performer nationwide: he improved by 28 percentage points on President Donald Trump’s 2024 margin in the state on his way to a nine-point win, the biggest swing in the continental United States. Bayh led a Democratic ticket that flipped a congressional seat, ousted the state House speaker, broke the GOP’s supermajority in the chamber and won the state comptroller’s office for the first time since the 1980s. His biggest gain came in rural Perry County, which Trump won by 30 points in 2024 and Bayh won by nine. The 6-foot-3 former Marine launched his campaign with a message of taking on corruption he said had festered at the statehouse after 16 years of one-party rule, and exit polls found voters ranked corruption as the single most important issue nationally. Vice President JD Vance called Bayh a “Trojan horse for radical Democrats,” a sign Republicans already see him as a future challenger.

articles.title: Here’s what Democrats and Trump could do together
articles.description: The new generation of Democrats storming into Washington wants to leave some of the partisanship behind, knowing it is the only way they might have a chance of accomplishing their campaign promises. The agenda includes funding the government by December 11, resolving the Iran war, overhauling environmental laws and repealing Trump’s tariffs. But the two sides will have to balance competing mandates from the midterms.
articles.body: The new generation of Democrats storming into Washington wants to leave some of the partisanship behind, CNN reports, knowing it is the only way they might have a chance of accomplishing any of their campaign promises. James Talarico, the Democrat elected to the US Senate from Texas, said he wants to make the remainder of Trump’s second term the most productive of his presidency, noting that “the American people cannot wait two years for change, so we must work with President Trump.” Abdul El-Sayed, the senator-elect from Michigan, suggested naming a public national health plan “Trumpcare for All” to entice the legacy-minded president. The potential common ground includes funding the federal government by December 11, resolving the Iran war, overhauling environmental laws to lower energy prices, undoing the Medicaid and Obamacare cuts, repealing Trump’s tariffs, raising the debt ceiling, fixing Social Security and Medicare, and addressing immigration and housing. But Democrats will have to balance competing mandates they won in November, and the window is narrow: Republicans still control the House and Senate for the rest of this year, and Democratic majorities take over on January 3.

articles.title: More than 46,000 UK music creators went LIVE on TikTok in 2026, with daily views up 74%
articles.description: More than 46,000 UK music creators have gone LIVE on TikTok in 2026, with daily views up 74% year-on-year, the company says. UK creators averaged 4.9 million global views a day on TikTok LIVE in September. The figures underline how central livestreaming has become to breaking new music.
articles.body: More than 46,000 UK music creators have gone LIVE on TikTok in 2026, according to the company, with daily views up 74% year-on-year. UK music creators averaged 4.9 million global views a day on TikTok LIVE in September. The numbers show how livestreaming has moved from a side feature to a central channel for artists to reach fans, test new material and build audiences in real time. For many emerging acts, a live session can now do the work that radio or a playlist add once did, and TikTok has been leaning into music-specific live features as part of that pitch. The figures also underline TikTok’s continued importance to the UK music industry even as the platform faces regulatory and competitive pressure on several fronts. Discovery on TikTok remains one of the fastest routes from obscurity to the charts, and live is becoming the format where that discovery increasingly happens.

articles.title: ByteDance sued by automotive photography firm EVOX, which says TikTok’s parent copied 7,095 images to train its Seedream AI
articles.description: ByteDance is being sued by California-based automotive photography firm EVOX, which alleges the TikTok parent copied 7,095 images to train its Seedream AI image generator. EVOX says it spent more than 30 years building a library of photographs covering several thousand vehicle makes and models. The case is the latest copyright fight over AI training data.
articles.body: ByteDance is being sued by automotive photography firm EVOX, which alleges TikTok’s parent copied 7,095 images to train its Seedream AI image generator, Music Business Worldwide reported. EVOX, based in California, says it has spent more than 30 years building a library of photographs covering several thousand vehicle makes and models, and that ByteDance used the images without permission to train its AI. The lawsuit is the latest in a growing wave of copyright cases against AI companies over training data, and it comes as the music industry fights its own battles on the same front: Reservoir recently expanded its copyright lawsuits against Suno and Anthropic to more than 2,500 songs combined. The EVOX case matters beyond photography because it tests whether scraping large libraries of creative work to train generative models is infringement, and the answer will shape how AI companies license — or pay for — the material they build on. ByteDance has not publicly responded to the specific allegations.

articles.title: Duetti secures $665 million to buy up more independent music catalogs
articles.description: Duetti, the music company backed by Jay-Z’s Roc Nation, has raised $665 million in fresh financing to accelerate its buying of independent artists’ catalogs. The package includes a $450 million asset-backed securitization led by Carlyle. Duetti has now raised more than $1.3 billion since 2022 and owns rights spanning over 50,000 masters and compositions.
articles.body: Duetti announced on Tuesday that it has secured $665 million in additional capital to accelerate investment in independent music catalogs. The financing package includes a $450 million asset-backed securitization anchored by global investment firm Carlyle, alongside $165 million of credit capacity from Viola Credit and a $50 million facility with Flexpoint Ford and Truist Bank. It is Duetti’s third asset-backed securitization in two years and more than five times larger than its inaugural deal in 2024, according to the Financial Times. Since it was founded in 2022, Duetti has completed more than 1,600 catalog investments and now owns a catalog of over 50,000 masters and compositions representing more than 3,000 recording artists from over 50 countries.
