He presided over the largest Mass of his pontificate, with around 2.5 million people in Buenos Aires, and was visibly moved on his return to Peru.
articles.body: Pope Leo XIV's visit to South America will go down as one of the lasting images of his papacy, CNN reports, drawing massive crowds and an emotional outpouring over his return to Peru just weeks after undergoing lung cancer surgery. More than 12 million people were estimated to have turned out for papal events and Masses in Uruguay, Argentina and Peru during the 12-day visit, according to Vatican estimates provided by local authorities. In Buenos Aires he presided over the largest Mass of his pontificate, with around 2.5 million people in attendance, and 3 million lined the streets of Lima for his return. The pope was visibly moved when he sang the Peruvian national anthem on his arrival in Lima and was seen wiping away tears during a gathering of young people in the national stadium. He kept up a dizzying schedule of dozens of speeches and events, dispelling, for now, lingering questions about his health, though he pointedly said he was still 'overcoming' his illness during a Mass outside Chiclayo last week. He even stayed in his former home in Chiclayo, the northern Peruvian city where he was bishop. The trip also revealed the missionary message of his papacy, with Leo emphasising his Peruvian identity — people in Peru see 'Papa Leon' as one of their own — and using the visit to send a message about the importance of voting, after his decision to cast a ballot in the US midterm elections.

articles.title: Gérard Depardieu drops appeal and accepts sexual assault conviction
articles.description: French actor Gérard Depardieu has dropped his appeal and accepted his sexual assault conviction, CNN reports. The decision ends the legal challenge to a verdict that was one of the most high-profile of France's #MeToo era.
articles.body: French actor Gérard Depardieu has dropped his appeal and accepted his sexual assault conviction, CNN reports, bringing an end to the legal challenge against one of the most high-profile verdicts of France's #MeToo era. The decision means the conviction now stands, closing a case that has divided French cultural life and tested the country's handling of sexual assault allegations against powerful figures in the arts. Depardieu, once one of France's most celebrated actors, has faced multiple allegations, and the conviction marked a turning point in how the French film industry confronts abuse. By dropping the appeal, he avoids a further public trial and the renewed scrutiny it would have brought, but the acceptance of the verdict is itself a significant moment. The news was among the top stories on CNN's homepage on Monday, alongside the bank outages and the AI chip curbs. No further details of the terms of the decision have been reported.

articles.title: Five EU countries unveil plans for a Rwanda deportation hub
articles.description: Five EU countries — Germany, Austria, Greece, Denmark and the Netherlands — have unveiled plans to create the first deportation hub outside the EU, in Rwanda, for migrants whose asylum claims have been rejected. The plan was reported by Reuters and picked up across European media on Monday.
articles.body: Five EU countries — Germany, Austria, Greece, Denmark and the Netherlands — have unveiled plans to create a deportation hub in Rwanda for migrants whose asylum claims have been rejected, CNN reports, in what would be the first such facility outside the European Union. The plan, first reported by Reuters, would see the five countries send rejected asylum seekers to a centre in Rwanda while their removal is arranged. It is the latest in a series of European efforts to externalise migration control, following earlier deals with countries including Turkey and Tunisia, and it echoes Britain's abandoned Rwanda deportation scheme. Supporters say the hub would deter irregular migration and speed up removals; critics argue it risks outsourcing the EU's responsibilities and exposing vulnerable people to harm. The announcement comes as migration remains one of the most divisive issues in European politics, with far-right parties gaining ground on the issue across the continent. The five countries have not yet given a timeline for the hub, and the legal basis for sending people to Rwanda is likely to be challenged in court. The plan was also covered by Ukrainska Pravda's European digest on Monday.

articles.title: California Governor Gavin Newsom visits Ukraine and announces medical supplies donation
articles.description: California Governor Gavin Newsom has visited Ukraine and announced a donation of medical supplies, CNN reports. The visit by one of America's most prominent Democratic governors comes as the war grinds on and US politics turns to the aftermath of the midterm elections.
articles.body: California Governor Gavin Newsom has visited Ukraine and announced a donation of medical supplies, CNN reports, in a trip that underlines the continuing American political engagement with Kyiv. Newsom, one of the most prominent Democratic governors in the United States, travelled to Ukraine as the war enters its fifth year and as US politics turns to the aftermath of the midterm elections, in which Democrats made gains. The donation of medical supplies is aimed at supporting Ukraine's overstretched hospitals, which have been treating the wounded from Russian strikes including the attack on the humanitarian aid point in Komyshuvakha. The visit also carries a political message: it signals that Democratic leaders intend to keep Ukraine high on the agenda even as the Trump administration pursues its own diplomacy with Moscow. Newsom has been increasingly visible on the national stage, and the Ukraine trip adds a foreign-policy dimension to his profile. No further details of the donation's size have been reported.

articles.title: Showdown looms over air traffic control meltdown as Trump blames Biden and Democrats warn of no blank cheque
articles.description: The fallout from Friday's nationwide FAA ground stop is escalating into a political showdown, with President Trump blaming the Biden administration on camera on Monday and demanding more money from Congress, while newly empowered Democrats warn there will be no blank cheque. Transport Secretary Sean Duffy toured Sunday talk shows demanding action — and turned friendly fire on fellow Republicans.
articles.body: The fallout from Friday's nationwide FAA ground stop is escalating into a political showdown, CNN reports, updating the story covered in the morning digest. President Trump, in his first on-camera comments about the situation on Monday, blamed the Biden administration and demanded more money from Congress, saying Friday's failure was caused by 'very, very old equipment that had a heart attack.' Transport Secretary Sean Duffy toured Sunday talk shows demanding action while assuring Americans they were safe in the air, and he and Trump turned friendly fire on fellow Republicans amid the blame game. Democrats, newly empowered after the midterms, warn there will be no blank cheque for air traffic control modernisation, and the issue is likely to become an early test of the hazardous political era that begins when Democrats run Congress next year opposite a GOP president. The meltdown was triggered by work to switch obsolete copper wire to modern fibre optics, apparently flooding the network with data; a senior administration official told CNN the work was at a remote FAA facility at South Arkansas Regional Airport in El Dorado, Arkansas. Duffy is asking Congress for $50 billion to finish modernising air traffic control, on top of $12.5 billion already allocated and on track to be spent by the end of 2028. A Government Accountability Office report from September warned the FAA has not developed a comprehensive lifecycle cost estimate for the new system. With Thanksgiving travel looming — the TSA expects to screen potentially more than 3 million passengers — officials warn another ground stop could happen again.

articles.title: Yamaha strikes $285M deal to acquire Disguise, whose visual tech powered tours by Bad Bunny, Beyoncé and Taylor Swift
articles.description: Yamaha has agreed a $285 million deal to acquire Disguise, the British company whose visual technology has powered tours by Bad Bunny, Beyoncé and Taylor Swift. Yamaha said it wants to 'move beyond the traditional boundaries of musical instruments and audio equipment.'
articles.body: Yamaha has struck a $285 million deal to acquire Disguise, the visual technology company whose systems have powered tours by Bad Bunny, Beyoncé and Taylor Swift, Music Business Worldwide reports. The Japanese instrument and audio giant said the acquisition reflects its ambition to 'move beyond the traditional boundaries of musical instruments and audio equipment' and into the live production technology that now defines arena-scale shows. Disguise's platform drives the giant LED walls, real-time graphics and immersive visuals that have become central to the biggest tours of the streaming era, where the stage show is as much a part of the product as the music. The deal is one of the largest music-technology acquisitions of the year and signals how instrument makers are repositioning themselves as broader live-entertainment companies. For the touring industry, it puts one of its key technology suppliers inside a deep-pocketed manufacturer with global distribution. The acquisition also comes as the live business continues to boom, with the biggest artists' tours now generating billions and production values escalating with every cycle.

articles.title: Suno launches Bridge, an app that drops AI stems into Ableton Live
articles.description: Suno has launched Bridge, an app that lets producers drop AI-generated stems straight into Ableton Live. At launch it works only with Ableton Live 12 on a Mac and requires a Suno Premier subscription.
articles.body: Suno has launched Bridge, an app that drops AI-generated stems directly into Ableton Live, Music Business Worldwide reports. The tool is aimed at producers who want to use Suno's AI music generation inside their existing workflow, rather than working in Suno's own interface. At launch, Bridge works only with Ableton Live 12 on a Mac, and it requires a Suno Premier subscription — a deliberately narrow rollout that suggests the company is testing the feature with its most committed users first. The launch comes as Suno faces expanding copyright lawsuits from Reservoir, which has now extended its claims to more than 2,500 songs, and from other rights holders. For Suno, Bridge is a pitch to working producers that its AI is a tool for professionals, not just a toy for casual users. For the wider industry, it is another step in the integration of AI generation into the standard production stack, raising fresh questions about how AI-assisted music should be credited and paid for. Whether producers embrace it will depend on the quality of the stems and on how the legal battles over AI training data play out.

articles.title: Reservoir expands copyright lawsuits against Suno and Anthropic to more than 2,500 songs combined
articles.description: Reservoir has expanded its copyright lawsuits against AI companies Suno and Anthropic to cover more than 2,500 songs combined, Music Business Worldwide reports. Reservoir first sued the two companies in October.
articles.body: Reservoir has expanded its copyright lawsuits against AI companies Suno and Anthropic to cover more than 2,500 songs combined, Music Business Worldwide reports. The music company first sued the two AI firms in October, and the expanded claims sharply raise the stakes of the litigation. The lawsuits allege that Suno and Anthropic used Reservoir's copyrighted songs to train their AI models without permission, part of a wave of legal action by music rights holders against AI companies. The expansion comes on the same day Suno launched Bridge, its new app for dropping AI stems into Ableton Live, underlining the tension between the AI companies' product ambitions and the music industry's determination to be paid for the work their models were trained on. The cases are among the most closely watched in the music business, because their outcome could set the terms for how AI companies license — or fail to license — the music they train on. If Reservoir prevails, it could force a licensing model on the AI industry; if it loses, the industry's leverage over AI firms will be much weaker. The suits are expected to take years to resolve.

articles.title: Jesús López to step down as chairman and CEO of Universal Music Latin America & Iberian Peninsula
articles.description: Jesús López is to step down as chairman and CEO of Universal Music Latin America & Iberian Peninsula, becoming chairman emeritus of GTS, Universal Music Group has announced. López has been working with UMG chief Sir Lucian Grainge on a succession plan, with details 'to be announced in due course.'
articles.body: Jesús López is to step down as chairman and CEO of Universal Music Latin America & Iberian Peninsula, becoming chairman emeritus of GTS, Universal Music Group has announced. López has been working with UMG chairman and CEO Sir Lucian Grainge on a succession plan, with details 'to be announced in due course', according to the company. The departure marks the end of an era for UMG's Latin American business, which López built into one of the most important divisions of the world's largest music company, riding the global explosion of Latin music. Under his leadership, UMG's Latin roster became a powerhouse, with the region's artists now regularly topping global charts. The succession will be closely watched in the Latin music world, where personal relationships and regional knowledge matter enormously. López's move to chairman emeritus of GTS, the live entertainment company, suggests he will remain involved in the business in a different capacity. UMG has not said when the change takes effect or who will succeed him.

articles.title: Sony Music renews multi-year licensing deal with China's NetEase Cloud Music
articles.description: Sony Music has renewed its multi-year licensing deal with China's NetEase Cloud Music, the companies announced on Friday, November 13. NetEase has now re-signed with all three major music companies in 2026.
articles.body: Sony Music has renewed its multi-year licensing deal with China's NetEase Cloud Music, Music Business Worldwide reports, in an agreement announced on Friday, November 13. The renewal means NetEase Cloud Music has now re-signed with all three major music companies in 2026, completing a clean sweep of the majors for one of China's largest streaming platforms. The deal matters because China is one of the fastest-growing recorded music markets in the world, and licensing terms there set the template for how Western music is monetised for hundreds of millions of Chinese listeners. For Sony, the renewal secures a key distribution channel for its artists in a market where streaming is dominated by local platforms rather than Spotify or Apple Music. For NetEase, having all three majors on board strengthens its hand against its main rival, Tencent Music, in the competition for subscribers. The terms of the deal have not been disclosed, but multi-year renewals with the majors are typically among the most valuable contracts in the streaming business.

articles.title: Symphonic inks deal to bring 'hundreds of thousands' of songs to Roblox
articles.description: Symphonic has signed a deal to bring 'hundreds of thousands' of songs to Roblox, Music Business Worldwide reports. Artists will receive royalties for all plays of their music on the platform, according to Symphonic.
articles.body: Symphonic has signed a deal to bring 'hundreds of thousands' of songs to Roblox, Music Business Worldwide reports, in the latest sign of how important gaming platforms have become for music discovery and revenue. According to Symphonic, artists will receive royalties for all plays of their music on Roblox, the platform where tens of millions of mostly young users spend hours every day. The deal gives Symphonic's independent artists and labels a new outlet at a moment when gaming and virtual worlds are becoming a major frontier for music, alongside streaming and social video. Roblox has already hosted virtual concerts by major artists, and its users routinely discover music inside games and experiences on the platform. For independent artists, who often struggle to get heard on crowded streaming services, a placement in Roblox can reach an audience that is hard to find elsewhere. The deal also reflects the growing professionalisation of music licensing in gaming, where platforms are increasingly expected to pay for the music their users hear.

articles.title: Peanuts music catalog owner settles copyright lawsuit against GameMill over Snoopy video game soundtrack
articles.description: The owner of the Peanuts music catalog has settled its copyright lawsuit against GameMill over the soundtrack of a Snoopy video game. The complaint alleged GameMill licensed the Peanuts characters but not Vince Guaraldi's music, then copied 'Linus and Lucy' and 'Skating'.
articles.body: The owner of the Peanuts music catalog has settled its copyright lawsuit against GameMill over the soundtrack of a Snoopy video game, Music Business Worldwide reports. The complaint alleged that GameMill licensed the Peanuts characters but not the music of Vince Guaraldi, the jazz pianist whose compositions — including 'Linus and Lucy' and 'Skating' — are inseparable from the Peanuts cartoons, and then copied those pieces for the game. The settlement brings to an end a dispute that highlighted the gap between licensing a brand's characters and licensing its music, two rights that are often held separately and can trip up even experienced games companies. Guaraldi's Peanuts music is among the most beloved in American popular culture, and the catalog owner's willingness to sue over it shows how seriously rights holders now police game soundtracks. The terms of the settlement have not been disclosed. For the games industry, the case is a reminder that a character licence does not automatically include the music associated with it — and that the music can be the more valuable asset.

articles.title: THE•TEAM forms 11-member board after Providence completes buyout of founder Casey Wasserman
articles.description: THE•TEAM has formed an 11-member board after Providence completed its buyout of founder Casey Wasserman. Seven of the board's members come from the company's leadership group, including CEO Michael Watts and CFO Elena Rochelli.
articles.body: THE•TEAM has formed an 11-member board after Providence completed its buyout of founder Casey Wasserman, Music Business Worldwide reports. Seven of the board's members come from the company's leadership group, including chief executive Michael Watts and chief financial officer Elena Rochelli, giving the management team a strong voice in the company's governance. The board's formation follows the completion of the Providence buyout, which saw the private equity firm buy out Wasserman, the founder of the Wasserman agency empire, in a deal that reshaped one of the most powerful companies in sports and entertainment representation. THE•TEAM is the holding company for the Wasserman agency's businesses, spanning sports, music and entertainment, and the new board will oversee its next phase of growth under Providence's ownership. The buyout and board formation mark the end of the Wasserman era at the company he built, and the beginning of a private-equity-led chapter. The industry will be watching whether the new structure changes how the agency competes for talent and deals.

articles.title: Lana Del Rey, Dua Lipa and Zara Larsson contribute new music to 'GTA VI: The Album'
articles.description: Lana Del Rey, Dua Lipa and Zara Larsson have contributed new music to 'GTA VI: The Album', Rolling Stone reports — new details on the soundtrack whose full 34-track list leaked online over the weekend. The game itself launches on Thursday, November 19.
articles.body: Lana Del Rey, Dua Lipa and Zara Larsson have contributed new music to 'GTA VI: The Album', Rolling Stone reports, adding fresh detail to the soundtrack story that dominated the weekend. The full 34-track list for the album leaked online when an image of its vinyl tracklist spread on Reddit and X, and Rolling Stone confirmed the image was legitimate — only 10 of the 34 tracks had been officially confirmed before the leak. The involvement of three major pop stars underlines how big a cultural event the game's release has become, with the soundtrack treated as a major music release in its own right rather than background audio. Grand Theft Auto VI launches on Thursday, November 19, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox, and it is the most anticipated game release in years, with analysts expecting it to break sales records. The album news follows a string of GTA VI stories this week, from the in-game 'Macca & Friends' cartoon series to reports that earning the platinum trophy could take around 200 hours. For the artists involved, a spot on the GTA VI soundtrack is now one of the most visible placements in popular music.

articles.title: Buffalo Springfield come together for the first time in many years
articles.description: Buffalo Springfield have come together for the first time in many years, Rolling Stone reports. Richie Furay talks about his upcoming documentary on the band, which features Neil Young, Stephen Stills, Cameron Crowe, David Geffen and Clive Davis.
articles.body: Buffalo Springfield have come together for the first time in many years, Rolling Stone reports, in a reunion that will delight fans of one of the most influential bands of the 1960s. Richie Furay, the band's co-founder, spoke to the magazine about his upcoming documentary on the group, which features Neil Young, Stephen Stills, Cameron Crowe, David Geffen and Clive Davis, among others. Buffalo Springfield lasted barely two years in their original incarnation, from 1966 to 1968, but their impact was enormous: they launched the careers of Young and Stills, produced the era-defining protest anthem 'For What It's Worth', and laid the groundwork for Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young. The band's members have rarely been in the same room since, making any coming-together a notable event. Furay's documentary promises to tell the story of the band from the inside, with the key players finally on record together. No details of the reunion's format — whether it involves a performance — have been reported, but the documentary alone is a major event for fans of the era.

articles.title: Wu-Tang Clan, Queen Latifah and MC Lyte inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame
articles.description: Wu-Tang Clan, Queen Latifah and MC Lyte were inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame on Saturday night at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, as hip-hop took the floor at the ceremony. Chris Rock inducted Wu-Tang Clan, whose living members crowded the stage for a medley including 'C.R.E.A.M.'.
articles.body: Wu-Tang Clan, Queen Latifah and MC Lyte were inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame on Saturday night at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, as hip-hop took the floor at the 2026 ceremony. Chris Rock inducted Wu-Tang Clan, and the Staten Island group's living members crowded the stage for a medley that included 'C.R.E.A.M.' and 'Wu-Tang Clan Ain't Nuthing ta F' Wit', according to Rolling Stone. RZA, the group's de facto leader, summed up the journey in his speech, reflecting on the group's rise from Staten Island to global influence. Queen Latifah and MC Lyte, two of the most important women in hip-hop history, were inducted alongside them, making it a landmark night for the genre's pioneers. The ceremony also saw Phil Collins inducted as a solo artist, with Cynthia Erivo and Travis Barker honouring him with a performance of 'In the Air Tonight'. The ceremony was not broadcast live, and an edited version airs on December 9 on ABC and Disney+. The inductions cap a year in which hip-hop's founding generation has finally received its due from the institution.

articles.title: Cynthia Erivo and Travis Barker honour Phil Collins with 'In the Air Tonight' at Rock Hall ceremony
articles.description: Cynthia Erivo and Travis Barker delivered a stunning tribute to Phil Collins at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame ceremony, performing a dramatic version of 'In the Air Tonight' with Barker playing the famous drum fill. Collins, 75, was inducted as a solo artist on Saturday and told the crowd: 'I'm really not as bad as it looks. I'm much better.'
articles.body: Cynthia Erivo and Travis Barker delivered a stunning tribute to Phil Collins at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony, performing a dramatic rendition of his 1980 hit 'In the Air Tonight', Rolling Stone reports. Erivo sang a slowed-down version of the song while Barker, the Blink-182 drummer, played the famous drum fill that is one of the most recognisable moments in pop music. The performance was one of the highlights of Saturday's ceremony at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, where Collins, 75, was inducted as a solo artist. Travis Barker delivered the induction speech, and Collins, who walked with two canes and did not perform, told the crowd: 'I'm really not as bad as it looks. I'm much better.' The tribute adds a fresh detail to the induction story covered in the morning digest, and it shows how the ceremony's performances have become as talked-about as the inductions themselves. Erivo and Barker are an unlikely duo, but their collaboration produced one of the most memorable moments of the night. The ceremony's edited broadcast airs on December 9 on ABC and Disney+.

articles.title: Rolling Stone UK Awards reveal Live Act and Festival nominees ahead of Thursday's ceremony
articles.description: The Rolling Stone UK Awards have revealed the nominees for the Live Act Award and the Festival Award, ahead of Thursday's ceremony at the Roundhouse in London. Danny Dyer returns as host, with four live performances and thirteen artists to be inducted into the Rolling Stone UK Hall of Fame.
articles.body: The Rolling Stone UK Awards have revealed the nominees for the Live Act Award, supported by ZYN, and the Festival Award, ahead of Thursday's ceremony at the Roundhouse in London. The two shortlists join the Group and Breakthrough fields already announced, with the ceremony taking place on November 19. Danny Dyer returns as host, and the night will include four live performances and the induction of thirteen artists into the Rolling Stone UK Hall of Fame. The Live Act Award recognises the artists who delivered the most memorable live shows of 2026, while the Festival Award honours the events that defined the summer. The nominees were announced nine days before the ceremony, and further category shortlists and performance details are expected in the days ahead. The awards, now in their latest edition, have become a fixture of the British music calendar, celebrating the year's standout UK and Irish acts. The full list of nominees for the remaining categories has not yet been published.

articles.title: Evanescence scores its first No. 1 on a Billboard chart with 'Who Will You Follow'
articles.description: Evanescence has finally reached No. 1 on a Billboard chart, as new single 'Who Will You Follow' debuts in first place on Hot Hard Rock Songs. It is the band's seventh career placement on the chart and its fifth top 10, and the track also leads the Hard Rock Digital Song Sales ranking.
articles.body: Evanescence has finally scored its first No. 1 on a Billboard chart, as new single 'Who Will You Follow' debuts in first place on this week's Hot Hard Rock Songs chart. The track also leads the Hard Rock Digital Song Sales ranking and debuts on more than half a dozen Billboard rankings in total. It is the band's seventh career placement on the Hot Hard Rock Songs chart and its fifth top 10, but its first time at the summit — a milestone that has eluded the group across a career spanning more than two decades, despite global hits like 'Bring Me to Life'. The chart success comes as the band continues to tour and release new material, and it shows the enduring commercial pull of a group that defined early-2000s rock. The single's strong debut across multiple charts suggests the new material is connecting with both the band's long-standing fanbase and a younger audience discovering them through streaming. For a band that has spent years as a reliable touring act, a first Billboard No. 1 is a late-career landmark worth noting.

articles.title: Ella Langley keeps 'Choosin' Texas' on top as Morgan Wallen climbs
articles.description: Ella Langley is still at No. 1 on Billboard's Hot Country Songs chart with 'Choosin' Texas', holding the top spot for another week. Morgan Wallen keeps building momentum behind 'Been By Now' at No. 3, while his new radio single 'Last Thing You Need' made a strong debut with 74 adds.
articles.body: Ella Langley is still sitting pretty at No. 1 with 'Choosin' Texas', holding the top spot for another week on Billboard's Hot Country Songs chart, according to the latest country chart update. Stella Lefty's 'Boston' sits at No. 2, while Morgan Wallen's 'Been By Now' holds at No. 3, continuing a strong run for the country superstar. At country radio, Wallen's 'Last Thing You Need' made a strong debut on Country Aircheck with 74 adds, giving it an immediate lift in the market. The same chart week also showed Zach Bryan's 'Lies' featuring Lana Del Rey, Luke Combs' 'Rethink Some Things' and Cody Johnson's 'Take Me Back (Leave Me There)' all staying in the conversation. Langley's hold on the top spot underlines her rapid rise in country music, where she has become one of the genre's most reliable hitmakers. The chart battle between Langley and Wallen is one of the most closely watched in country music right now, with both artists commanding huge streaming numbers and radio support.

articles.title: Blue Öyster Cult's '(Don't Fear) The Reaper' tops a Billboard chart 50 years later, thanks to Reacher
articles.description: Blue Öyster Cult's '(Don't Fear) The Reaper', which peaked at No. 12 on the Hot 100 in November 1976, has claimed the top spot on Billboard's Top TV Songs chart 50 years later, thanks to its appearance in the Prime Video series Reacher. The song generated 11.8 million US on-demand streams and 1,000 downloads this fall.
articles.body: A rock song that never quite reached the top of the Billboard Hot 100 in 1976 has finally found its way to No. 1 on a Billboard chart, 50 years after its original release. Blue Öyster Cult's '(Don't Fear) The Reaper', which peaked at No. 12 on the Hot 100 in November 1976, has claimed the top spot on Billboard's Top TV Songs chart, thanks to its appearance in the Prime Video series Reacher. The monthly chart, powered by Tunefind, ranks songs featured in television shows using a formula that incorporates song and show data along with streaming and sales figures tracked by Luminate. According to Billboard, '(Don't Fear) The Reaper' generated 11.8 million US on-demand streams and 1,000 downloads this fall, helping propel the nearly 50-year-old recording to No. 1. The song spent 20 weeks on the Hot 100 in 1976, peaking during the chart weeks ending November 6 and 13 of that year. More recently it appeared in Netflix's Wednesday, while its use in Reacher helped bring it back to the Billboard charts in 2026. It was also featured in promotional material for the upcoming Friday the 13th prequel series Crystal Lake. Fifty years after it first reached No. 12, Blue Öyster Cult's biggest hit has finally reached No. 1.

articles.title: BigXthaPlug hits No. 1 on Billboard's Top Rap Albums with 'Better Over Time'
articles.description: BigXthaPlug has hit No. 1 on Billboard's Top Rap Albums chart with 'Better Over Time', in the chart week dated November 14. The Dallas rapper's album also reached No. 7 on the all-genre Billboard 200, matching his career best, and No. 2 on Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums.
articles.body: BigXthaPlug has hit No. 1 on Billboard's Top Rap Albums chart with 'Better Over Time', in the chart week dated November 14, 2026. The Dallas rapper's album also reached No. 2 on Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums, a new career high, and No. 7 on the all-genre Billboard 200, matching his best showing there. Billboard also counted 10 tracks from the album on Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs, underlining how deeply the project has penetrated the charts. The album was released through BigXthaPlug's own imprint in partnership with UnitedMasters, the independent distribution platform, making the No. 1 a notable win for the independent route. BigXthaPlug has built his career on a relentless release schedule and a direct connection with his audience, and 'Better Over Time' is his biggest commercial success yet. The chart-topping week caps a strong year for the rapper, who has become one of the most consistent hitmakers in Southern hip-hop.

articles.title: Levi's joins Billboard Canada Women in Music 2026 as official partner
articles.description: Levi's has joined Billboard Canada Women in Music 2026 as an official partner, ahead of the celebration on November 24 at REBEL in Toronto. Scarborough-born R&B artist Chxrry will receive this year's Rising Star Award, and the night will honour Cardi B, Bebe Rexha, Summer Walker, Tia Wood and Faouzia.
articles.body: Levi's has joined Billboard Canada Women in Music 2026 as an official partner, Billboard Canada announced on Monday. The celebration takes place on November 24 at REBEL in Toronto, and the partnership will celebrate emerging talent and personal style through the Rising Star Award presented by Levi's and a red-carpet style segment. Scarborough-born R&B artist Chxrry will receive this year's Rising Star honour. Now in its third year, Billboard Canada Women in Music brings together artists and industry leaders for an evening of performances and awards, and the 2026 celebration will honour women making an impact in Canada and around the world, including Cardi B, Bebe Rexha, Summer Walker, Tia Wood and Faouzia. The partnership is a natural fit for Levi's, which has long been associated with music culture, and it underlines how brand partnerships have become central to music awards events. Tickets and event information are available through Billboard Canada's channels.

articles.title: Ukrainian forces strike the Crimean Bridge overnight, halting traffic; Kremlin calls the damage 'minor'
articles.description: Ukrainian forces struck the Crimean Bridge overnight, halting vehicle traffic from around 02:00 Moscow time, and the occupation governor said traffic would be restricted until about midday while four passenger trains to Crimea were delayed. The Kremlin later called the damage 'minor' and said traffic continues. The 19-km bridge is Russia's only direct land link to occupied Crimea and a key supply route for its forces.
articles.body: Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge overnight, and the head of annexed Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, said the enemy had struck the bridge, with vehicle traffic restricted until around midday. Traffic was stopped from about 02:00 Moscow time, four passenger trains bound for Crimea were delayed by two to four and a half hours, and an operational headquarters was set up in Kerch. Monitoring channels reported a hit on one of the arches of the navigable span, and Russia's transport ministry said there were no casualties, though the scale of the damage was not disclosed. Russia's defence ministry claimed its air defences shot down 1,336 Ukrainian drones overnight across 17 regions and two seas. The bridge has been attacked several times since 2022, most seriously by a truck bomb in October 2022, and the strike follows months of intensified Russian attacks on bridges inside Ukraine, including in Kyiv. Ukraine's defence forces did not comment on the reported strike. Update (midday): rail traffic across the bridge had resumed, but the road section stayed closed while officials assessed the damage; Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin said the timeline for full restoration would be announced after the assessment, and the transport ministry was weighing reopening the road in alternating directions.

articles.title: Hundreds of thousands march in Prague in the biggest protest in modern Czech history, defending public media
articles.description: Hundreds of thousands of people marched in Prague on Sunday, November 15, against government plans to change the funding of public broadcast media. The demonstration in Letná park, organised by the 'Million Moments for Democracy' movement, drew more than 350,000 people by the organisers' count, making it the largest rally in modern Czech history.
articles.body: On Sunday, November 15, hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets of Prague to protest against the government's plans to change the financing of public broadcast media, gathering in the capital's Letná park. The action was organised by the 'Million Moments for Democracy' movement, which estimated the crowd at more than 350,000 people and called it the largest rally in the modern history of Czechia. The protest defends the independence of public service media against funding changes that critics say would expose broadcasters to political pressure. The scale of the mobilisation recalls the mass demonstrations of the Velvet Revolution era, and it marks the biggest civic protest the country has seen in decades. The march was peaceful, and its size alone makes it a significant political moment for the Czech government, which now faces a broad public backlash over its media plans.

articles.title: UN states want limits on autonomous AI weapons; Russia and the US are expected to oppose talks, Reuters reports
articles.description: UN member states meet in Geneva on Monday, November 16, to decide whether to start negotiations on international rules for autonomous weapons, systems based on artificial intelligence that can kill without human involvement. Most of the 128 states in the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons back new rules, but the leading military powers, including the US, Russia and Israel, oppose them, diplomatic sources told Reuters.
articles.body: On Monday, November 16, a meeting of the countries party to the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons opens in Geneva, bringing together 128 states to decide whether to begin negotiations on international rules governing autonomous weapons. The weapons in question are AI-based systems capable of killing without human participation, and the debate is about whether they should be restricted or banned under international law. Most of the states in the convention support developing new rules, but the leading military powers, including the United States, Russia and Israel, oppose them, according to diplomatic sources cited by Reuters. In September, the US and Russia already succeeded in softening a draft international agreement on autonomous weapons, watering down its provisions. The Geneva meeting is therefore a test of whether the majority of states can move the process forward despite opposition from the countries with the most advanced military AI programmes, and its outcome will shape the prospects for any binding global regime on killer robots.

articles.title: Moldova calls federalisation 'an idea pulled out of mothballs' as Russia is reported to demand it in the Ukraine talks
articles.description: Moldova's parliament speaker Igor Grosu said the country's European course is fixed in the constitution and dismissed the ideas Russia is promoting as 'pulled out of mothballs'. He was responding to reports by Bild and Ekho that Russia is demanding, in the Ukraine war negotiations, that Moldova be turned into a federation including Transnistria and Gagauzia.
articles.body: The speaker of Moldova's parliament, Igor Grosu, has rejected the idea of federalising the country, calling it an idea 'pulled out of mothballs' and stressing that Moldova's European course is enshrined in the constitution. He was commenting on publications by Bild and the outlet Ekho, which reported on November 12 that several negotiating groups are involved in the process of ending the Russia-Ukraine war and that among Russia's conditions is the transformation of Moldova into a federal republic that would also include Transnistria and Gagauzia. The demand, if real, would reach far beyond Ukraine itself, echoing the maximalist list of Russian conditions for ending the war that was published in the media over the weekend and covers the EU, NATO, Moldova, Finland and Central Asia. Grosu's blunt dismissal signals that Chisinau has no intention of entertaining a settlement imposed through the Ukraine talks, and it underlines how the peace diplomacy is spilling over into the politics of Russia's neighbours.

articles.title: Ukrainian forces strike the Crimean Bridge overnight, halting traffic; Kremlin calls the damage 'minor'
articles.description: The Crimean Bridge was struck on November 16, 2026, disrupting vehicle traffic between occupied Crimea and Russia. Kerch authorities deployed an operational headquarters and response services, while Russian officials acknowledged damage and said restoration timelines would be determined later. Ukrainian defence forces did not comment on the reported attack.
articles.body: The Crimean Bridge was struck on November 16, 2026, disrupting vehicle traffic between occupied Crimea and Russia, according to the occupation governor Sergei Aksyonov, who said the enemy had hit the bridge and traffic would be restricted until around midday. Kerch authorities deployed an operational headquarters and emergency services to deal with the consequences, and four passenger trains to Crimea were delayed. Russia's transport ministry said there were no casualties and that railway traffic continued as normal, while the Kremlin later described the damage as minor. The 19-km bridge over the Kerch Strait is the only direct link between Russia's transport network and the Crimean peninsula, which Russia seized and annexed in 2014, and it has been a key supply route for Russian forces in Ukraine. It has come under attack several times since 2022, and the overnight strike followed an intensification of Russian attacks on bridges in Ukraine in recent months, including in Kyiv. Ukrainian defence forces did not comment on the reported strike. Update (midday): rail traffic across the bridge had resumed, but the road section stayed closed while officials assessed the damage; Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin said the timeline for full restoration would be announced after the assessment, and the transport ministry was weighing reopening the road in alternating directions.

articles.title: Russia launches 158 drones at Ukraine overnight; Kyiv reports a record 2,560 Russian troops lost in one day
articles.description: Russia launched 158 strike drones at Ukraine from the evening of November 15 into the morning of November 16, and Ukrainian air defences neutralised 131 of them by 08:00, including 55 jet-powered drones. Direct hits were recorded at 19 locations and debris fell at 11 more, with power outages in Kirovohrad region. Ukraine's General Staff also reported 2,560 Russian personnel killed or wounded in the past day, above the previous daily record of 2,500.
articles.body: Russia began a large drone attack on Ukraine at 18:00 on November 15, launching 158 strike drones, including 77 Shahed-type drones, and the assault continued through the night. By 08:00 on November 16, Ukraine's air force said 131 drones had been shot down or suppressed, 55 of them jet-powered, though several drones remained airborne and combat operations continued. Direct impacts were recorded at 19 sites and falling debris at 11 locations, with people injured, homes and infrastructure damaged and power cuts reported in several regions, including Kirovohrad. Separately, Ukraine's General Staff reported 2,560 Russian troops killed or wounded over the preceding day, exceeding the previously cited daily record of 2,500, bringing total estimated Russian personnel losses since the invasion to about 1,625,420. The figures remain subject to clarification by the General Staff. The overnight barrage came hours after Ukraine's strike on the Crimean Bridge, underlining that neither side is easing the long-range war even as peace diplomacy intensifies.

articles.title: Budanov and Arakhamia pursue two parallel tracks on Donbas in the peace talks
articles.description: Kyrylo Budanov and Davyd Arakhamia, key figures in Ukraine's negotiating delegation, are promoting distinct approaches to the Donbas question within the same delegation. Both maintain parallel contacts with Russian and US officials while operating under President Zelenskyy's shared directives.
articles.body: Two of the most prominent members of Ukraine's peace delegation, intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov and parliamentary faction leader Davyd Arakhamia, are advancing different approaches to resolving the Donbas question, even as they work inside the same team. Both maintain parallel contacts with Russian and American officials, operating under President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's shared directives but pushing distinct lines on the territory Russia has failed to fully conquer. The split comes days after Zelenskyy revealed the US had, for the first time, asked whether Ukraine would leave Donbas in exchange for NATO membership, a proposal that would trade land for alliance membership. The existence of two tracks suggests Kyiv is hedging between positions as the diplomacy enters its most active phase in months, with Trump's envoys recently back from Moscow and a possible trilateral meeting looming. No details of the two approaches have been published yet, and it is unclear whether they reflect a deliberate good-cop, bad-cop division of labour or a genuine disagreement inside the delegation.

articles.title: EU Council approves nearly €8 billion ninth payment to Ukraine, the largest single disbursement yet
articles.description: The Council of the European Union approved a nearly €8 billion ninth payment to Ukraine under the Ukraine Facility on November 16. It is the largest single disbursement under the programme and will support macroeconomic stability, recovery, reforms and Ukraine's public administration.
articles.body: The Council of the European Union approved a nearly €8 billion ninth payment to Ukraine under the Ukraine Facility on November 16, the largest single disbursement under the programme so far. The money is intended to support macroeconomic stability, recovery, reforms and the functioning of Ukraine's public administration as the war grinds on. The payment lands as the European Commission has separately proposed a €45 billion loan for Ukraine, guaranteed by the EU's common budget, with four member states resisting the plan. The financing debate is intensifying as the cost of the war mounts and as EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas urges the bloc to seek a ceasefire before engaging in detailed talks on Moscow's demands. The disbursement is a concrete signal that, whatever the arguments over the next funding package, the EU's existing support pipeline for Kyiv is still flowing at full scale.

articles.title: Estonia to close all Russia border crossings from December 1 after a failed sabotage attempt on a drone maker
articles.description: Estonia will close all of its border crossings with Russia from December 1, following a failed arson attempt on the Estonian drone manufacturer Threod Systems, which Estonian authorities blame on Russia and its intelligence services. Ukraine expressed full solidarity with Estonia and called for a coordinated European response to Russian sabotage.
articles.body: Estonia will close all border crossing points with the Russian Federation from December 1, in response to a failed arson attempt against the Estonian drone manufacturer Threod Systems. Estonian authorities attribute the sabotage attempt to Russia and its intelligence services, and the border closure is the most sweeping response yet to a campaign of suspected Russian sabotage across Europe. Ukraine expressed full solidarity with Estonia and urged European countries to take coordinated measures against Russian diversions. The decision comes amid a wave of incidents linked to Moscow, including bomb threats that have left European authorities searching for answers, and it underlines how the war's shadow war of sabotage and intimidation is pushing frontline states towards harder security measures. The closure will sever one of the last overland links between the EU and Russia, with consequences for cross-border trade and travel that Tallinn has evidently decided are worth the security gain.

articles.title: Kaja Kallas: EU must seek a ceasefire before detailed talks with Russia; Moscow's demands are 'absurd'
articles.description: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on November 16 that Russian demands for ending the war in Ukraine are absurd and designed to prolong the fighting. She urged the EU negotiating team to secure a ceasefire before discussing Moscow's demands and to put forward its own maximalist demands, backed by sanctions and frozen Russian assets.
articles.body: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on November 16 that Russian demands for ending the war in Ukraine are absurd and designed to prolong the fighting rather than end it. She urged the EU negotiating team to secure a ceasefire before discussing Moscow's demands in detail, and to put forward its own maximalist demands, backed by sanctions and frozen Russian assets. The intervention comes as the peace diplomacy enters its most active phase in months, with media publishing a list of Putin's maximalist conditions that reach far beyond Ukraine to cover the EU, NATO, Moldova, Finland and Central Asia. Kallas's position is that Europe should not negotiate the terms of a settlement while Russia is still fighting, and that the bloc's leverage lies in economic pressure rather than concessions. Her stance aligns with President Macron's warning that an unjust peace in Ukraine would be a recipe for a new war, and it sets up a tension with the US-led push for a quick deal.

articles.title: At least 57 killed in a Russian strike on a humanitarian aid distribution site in Komyshuvakha
articles.description: At least 57 people were killed in a Russian strike on a humanitarian aid distribution point in Komyshuvakha, in an attack on November 15 that was not covered in yesterday's digest. The strike hit a site where civilians were collecting humanitarian aid, making it one of the deadliest single attacks on civilians in recent weeks.
articles.body: At least 57 people were killed in a Russian strike on a humanitarian aid distribution point in Komyshuvakha, according to reports from November 15 that emerged after yesterday's digest was compiled. The attack struck a site where civilians had gathered to collect humanitarian aid, and the death toll makes it one of the deadliest single Russian attacks on civilians in recent weeks. The strike fits a pattern of Russian attacks on civilian infrastructure and gathering points that has continued even as peace talks intensify, and it comes days after Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia injured 15 people, including children. The scale of the killing at an aid distribution point, a site with no military value, is likely to draw international condemnation and to harden Kyiv's position that a ceasefire must come before any discussion of territorial or political concessions. Ukrainian officials have not yet released a full casualty breakdown, and the toll may rise as rescue work continues.

articles.title: Svitolina loses the WTA Finals final to Mirra Andreeva, 7:5, 6:3
articles.description: Elina Svitolina lost the WTA Finals 2026 final to Mirra Andreeva, 7:5, 6:3, in a match played on November 15. Svitolina had reached the season-ending final for the third time in her career after thrashing Linda Noskova in the semi-final, but the debutante Andreeva took the title.
articles.body: Elina Svitolina lost the final of the WTA Finals 2026 to Mirra Andreeva, going down 7:5, 6:3 in the championship match. Svitolina had reached the final of the season-ending tournament for the third time in her career, after thrashing Linda Noskova to get there, but she could not overcome the young Andreeva, who won the title on her debut appearance at the event. The defeat is a disappointment for Ukraine's leading player, who had been in strong form throughout the tournament, but reaching a third WTA Finals final remains a significant achievement in her career. Andreeva's victory caps a breakthrough season for the teenager, who is now established among the very top of the women's game. The final was played in Indian Wells, where the tournament was held this year.

articles.title: Rockstar shows a teaser for the 'Macca & Friends' cartoon series, watchable only inside GTA VI
articles.description: Rockstar Games has published a teaser trailer for the animated series 'Macca & Friends'. All episodes will be available from November 19 on the in-game WEAZEL television channel inside Grand Theft Auto VI.
articles.body: Rockstar Games has published a teaser trailer for the animated series 'Macca & Friends', a cartoon that will exist only inside Grand Theft Auto VI. All episodes of the series will be available from November 19 on the WEAZEL television channel, the in-game broadcaster players can watch inside the game world. The move is a classic Rockstar touch, building out the satirical media landscape of Leonida, the game's fictional Florida, with original animated programming rather than licensed content. It also shows how much of the game's identity Rockstar is investing in its in-world media, alongside the 34-track official soundtrack album and Justice's separate 50-song score. The teaser arrived just days before launch, as preloading began on PS5 and the game was confirmed to take up 115 GB. GTA VI launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

articles.title: God of War: Sons of Sparta comes to PlayStation 4 today, with a free update adding two new modes
articles.description: Sony Interactive Entertainment has officially released the 2D action game God of War: Sons of Sparta on PlayStation 4 today, November 16. The spin-off, developed by Mega Cat Studios and Santa Monica Studio, arrives on the last-generation console alongside a free content update with two new modes.
articles.body: Sony Interactive Entertainment has officially announced the release of the two-dimensional action game God of War: Sons of Sparta on PlayStation 4, with the game arriving on the last-generation console on November 16. The spin-off, developed by Mega Cat Studios and Santa Monica Studio, was originally released on February 12 on PlayStation 5, and it was announced together with the remake of the first God of War trilogy. The PS4 version launches simultaneously with a free content update that adds two new modes to the game on both PS4 and PS5. Bringing a 2026 release to a console two generations old is an unusual move, and it reflects Sony's willingness to keep the large PS4 installed base served with new first-party content even as the PS5 generation matures. The game is a 2D take on Kratos, a sharp departure from the series' recent third-person epics.

articles.title: DOOM: The Dark Ages gets 'Slaughter Mode' today, a free endless-wave trial for Revelations owners
articles.description: Bethesda has released the new Slaughter Mode update for DOOM: The Dark Ages today, November 16, on consoles and PC. The free mode, an endless-wave survival trial, is available to all owners of the Revelations expansion.
articles.body: Bethesda Softworks has published a trailer for the new update for DOOM: The Dark Ages, which arrives on November 16 on consoles and PC. The developers at id Software have prepared Slaughter Mode, or 'Boyne', an endless trial designed to test the most experienced Doom Slayers. In the mode, players face infinitely advancing waves of enemies, fighting round after round against ever-growing numbers of foes and bosses on randomised arenas, aiming to set new records and unlock cosmetic rewards. To play Slaughter Mode you need the Revelations expansion, the Premium Edition of DOOM: The Dark Ages, or the Premium Upgrade. The update lands in the same week as the GTA VI launch, giving Doom players something new to chew on while the industry's attention is elsewhere, and it continues Bethesda's post-launch support for the game, which arrived earlier in 2026 to strong reviews.

articles.title: Nintendo introduces digital game gifting for Switch 2 family groups ahead of the holidays
articles.description: Nintendo has announced a gifting system that lets users give digital versions of games to members of their Switch 2 family group. The holiday-timed eShop update goes live on November 16 and covers selected games, add-ons and content bundles.
articles.body: Nintendo has announced a gifting system that allows users to give digital versions of games to members of their Switch 2 family group, with the holiday-timed eShop update going live on November 16. The system covers selected games, add-ons and content bundles, and the company notes that some digital products may not be available as gifts. Each console user can create a family group and add up to eight members, then send a gift by finding a game in the eShop, choosing the 'Gift' icon on its page, picking a recipient and a console to send it to, and selecting gift wrapping before completing the purchase as normal. Child-controlled accounts cannot send gifts, and there is a limit on the number of digital items that can be gifted within a given period. Gifts are delivered to the recipient immediately, so buyers need to be sure before confirming. The feature arrives just ahead of the holiday season, when gifting is at its peak, and it closes a long-standing gap with rival storefronts that have offered game gifting for years.

articles.title: PS Plus Extra and Premium November games revealed: Death Stranding 2 headlines, available from November 17
articles.description: Sony Interactive Entertainment has published the list of games coming in November to PlayStation Plus Extra, Deluxe and Premium subscribers. The flagship of the lineup is last year's Death Stranding 2: On the Beach from Hideo Kojima, and the games become available on November 17.
articles.body: Sony Interactive Entertainment has published the list of games that will become available in November to subscribers of the extended PlayStation Plus plans. The flagship of the lineup is Death Stranding 2: On the Beach, last year's game from Hideo Kojima, which headlines the Extra tier on PS5. The Premium and Deluxe tiers also get Soul Reaver 2, the classic action-adventure, among other titles. The new games start rolling out on November 17. The lineup is a strong one for subscribers, putting a major recent first-party release into the catalogue just over a year after launch, and it arrives in a crowded week that also brings the GTA VI launch and the Game Awards nominees announcement on November 17. For PS5 owners who have not yet played Kojima's sequel, the Extra tier now offers the cheapest route in.

articles.title: Riot Games announces League of Legends: New Dawn, a major overhaul of the game, with a full reveal in January 2027
articles.description: Riot Games has officially announced League of Legends: New Dawn, a major rework of the 17-year-old MOBA, with a full presentation planned for January 2027. The first teaser aired during the World Championship 2026 final, where Bilibili Gaming beat Gen.G 3–1 to take the title. Riot has given no details yet on what New Dawn changes, but the name signals the biggest shake-up of the game in years.
articles.body: Riot Games officially announced the League of Legends: New Dawn project on November 15, with the first teaser shown during the World Championship 2026 final in which Bilibili Gaming beat Gen.G 3–1 to win their first title. A full presentation of the game is planned for January 2027. Riot has not yet said what New Dawn actually is — whether a new client, a rebuilt game, a new mode or a full relaunch — only that it is a major new project for the franchise, which launched in 2009 and remains the world's biggest esport. The announcement lands as League of Legends heads into its 18th year, with Riot under pressure to modernise a game whose client and onboarding have long been criticised even as its competitive scene keeps breaking viewership records. More details are expected in the January reveal, and the project will be watched closely by the millions of players who have stayed with the game since its early years.

articles.title: AI bubble will likely burst and cause a recession before the 2028 election, Wall Street's former top cop says
articles.description: The AI boom is a bubble that will likely burst and cause a recession before the 2028 presidential election, former SEC chair Gary Gensler told CNN. 'It's already a bubble,' said Gensler, pointing to an estimated $800 billion a year being poured into building AI infrastructure.
articles.body: The artificial intelligence boom is a bubble that will likely burst and cause a recession prior to the 2028 presidential election, Gary Gensler, the former top cop on Wall Street, told CNN. Gensler, who led the Securities and Exchange Commission from 2021 until 2025 and is now a professor at MIT, pointed to the mind-boggling amounts of money, by some estimates $800 billion a year, being plowed into building AI infrastructure. His warning comes at a precarious moment for the industry after a cascading series of shocks: Democrats' midterm victories raised fears of a crackdown on the data centers at the heart of the AI buildout, Nvidia's Jensen Huang fell in a spy scandal, and Anthropic is attempting a record-shattering IPO. Gensler said the first dominoes would fall among the neoclouds, debt-laden firms leasing supercomputing power, where 'we're going to see some breakage and bankruptcies,' a view Elon Musk echoed by warning of 'guppy-level death and consolidation' among the 200-plus neoclouds. He expects a downturn 'as significant as' the dot-com bust but not as harsh as the 2008 subprime meltdown, arriving before November 2028. Others disagree: Yardeni Research's Ed Yardeni called it a self-correcting bubble, saying 'the air is coming out' without a burst, and noted chipmaker valuations have already fallen below the broader market.

articles.title: Trump's redistricting gambit backfired: Republicans won only 2 of the 15 districts they tried to rig
articles.description: Republicans won only 2 of the 15 districts they tried to rig for themselves in Trump's mid-decade redistricting push, according to CNN's redistricting tracker. Democrats could gain a net 16 seats from the redrawn states, with the GOP losing 4 of the 5 Texas seats it gerrymandered and North Carolina's map letting Democrats flip at least half a dozen GOP seats.
articles.body: When President Donald Trump launched his mid-decade redistricting gambit in Texas last year, he confidently declared that Republicans were 'entitled to five more seats' in the Lone Star State. In last week's election, the party lost 4 of the 5 Texas seats it gerrymandered for itself, and it was not just Texas: Republicans have won only 2 of the 15 districts they tried to rig for themselves, according to CNN's redistricting tracker, with one more seat, in Louisiana, going to a runoff. All told, the gambit actually cost them seats, after the map they redrew in North Carolina spread the party too thin and allowed Democrats to flip at least a half-dozen GOP seats. The GOP gained one seat in Texas and another in Tennessee, but Democrats are set to flip five seats in California, six or seven in North Carolina and three in Ohio, plus a seat in Utah from a court-ordered redraw. If current results hold, Democrats could gain a net of 16 seats from the states that were redrawn. The prevailing narrative is that the gambit backfired badly, though CNN notes it is too early to say it will not help Republicans over the long term, and attempted Republican redraws could have jeopardised additional districts in South Carolina and Indiana.

articles.title: Trump heads to Asia for ASEAN and APEC, with a historic three-way meeting with Xi and Putin on Thursday
articles.description: President Donald Trump departs Monday for the Philippines, then the ASEAN summit in Manila and APEC in Shenzhen, punctuated Thursday by an unprecedented three-way meeting with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin on nuclear non-proliferation. The trip follows the midterm rebuke, a West Wing shake-up and calls from some allies to fire cabinet members.
articles.body: President Donald Trump will attempt to follow a long tradition of presidents using foreign trips to leave political upheaval behind, departing Monday for a long-planned swing through Asia. He will attend the ASEAN summit in Manila and the APEC summit in Shenzhen, where Thursday brings an unprecedented three-way meeting with his authoritarian counterparts from China and Russia, focused on nuclear non-proliferation, a rare trilateral format bringing together the leaders of the world's three biggest nuclear powers. The sharp rebuke Trump faced from voters this month was quickly noted by foreign counterparts watching for signs of fading political capital, and he will be joined by Elon Musk, whose $445 million in political spending failed to deliver Republican majorities. The scandal involving Jensen Huang's AI chips and affair with an alleged Chinese spy will loom over the visit to Shenzhen, though Trump does not intend to raise the spying matter with Xi, with whom he will meet for the fourth time in just over a year. Trump also plans to sign a trade agreement with Thailand this week as he looks to counter the narrative of declining power with commercial deals. An air travel meltdown before he left, which Trump did not address publicly for days, also raised questions about his focus heading into the trip.

articles.title: Another FAA ground stop could happen again ahead of Thanksgiving, as Duffy asks Congress for $50 billion
articles.description: More than a million people were stranded at airports on Friday after the FAA grounded all planes nationwide for the second time since 9/11, and with the busiest travel season ahead, officials warn it could happen again. The cause was the switch from old copper wire to fibre optics, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy is now asking Congress for $50 billion to finish modernising air traffic control.
articles.body: More than a million people were stranded at airports across the country on Friday after the agency in charge of transporting passengers safely had to ground all planes, just two weeks before the start of the busiest travel season of the year. For just the second time since the September 11, 2001 attacks, the Federal Aviation Administration grounded aircraft nationwide, citing extraordinary circumstances and reasons of safety. During a news conference over the weekend, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that at at least one remote FAA location, contractor L3Harris was doing routine maintenance to switch telecommunication lines from an old copper wire to modern fibre optics, and it remains unclear whether contractor error or faulty equipment during the switch caused the meltdown. The FAA will investigate. The agency has been replacing the country's dated copper wiring since at least 2025, and Duffy said the transition has to happen, while upping his ask to Congress for $50 billion to complete the work. The FAA has so far replaced 69% of copper communication lines with high-speed fibre, using $12.5 billion from the president's spending bill last year. The disruption cascaded for days as airlines repositioned crews and planes, and the Transportation Security Administration expects to screen potentially more than 3 million passengers nationwide over Thanksgiving. A Government Accountability Office report from September found the FAA has not developed a comprehensive lifecycle cost estimate for the modernisation.

articles.title: See dazzling meteors from the Leonid shower this week, peaking overnight Monday into Tuesday
articles.description: Each November, Earth passes through debris left by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, creating the annual Leonid meteor shower. This year it is expected to peak overnight from Monday through Tuesday, when up to 15 meteors per hour could be visible under clear conditions.
articles.body: Each November, Earth passes through a trail of debris left behind by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, creating the annual celestial display known as the Leonid meteor shower. This year, the shower is expected to peak overnight from Monday through Tuesday, when Earth passes through the densest part of the debris trail, according to the American Meteor Society. Under clear conditions, sky-gazers could see up to 15 meteors per hour, said Bill Cooke, lead of NASA's Meteoroid Environment Office. The best time to spot these fleeting meteors will be in the early morning hours, around 2 or 3 a.m., in any time zone. The moon, in its waxing crescent phase and 39% illuminated, will have set by that time, leaving darker skies for viewing. The Leonids will be visible from both the Northern and Southern hemispheres, although the constellation Leo appears lower in the sky south of the equator. Scientists expect the next Leonid meteor storm to occur in 2033, but watching this year's shower still offers a unique opportunity to connect with the cosmos. Meteors from the Leonids will be visible until the shower ends on November 30, and the Geminids follow on December 13-14.

articles.title: Billboard changes its free vs paid streaming formula, and YouTube is bringing its data back to the charts
articles.description: Billboard is narrowing the ratio between paid subscription streams and ad-supported streams from 1:2.5 to 1:1.5, so 1,000 paid streams or 1,500 ad-supported streams will equal one album unit on the Billboard 200 from the charts dated January 16, 2027. YouTube confirmed the same day that its data will return to Billboard's US charts in 2027.
articles.body: YouTube is returning to Billboard's US charts, following a change by Billboard to how it weights paid subscription streams against ad-supported streams, the issue that led YouTube to withdraw its data in January. Billboard announced the change on Monday, November 9, and YouTube confirmed its return later the same day. Billboard is narrowing the ratio between paid subscription streams and ad-supported streams from 1:2.5 to 1:1.5, so under the new formula, 1,000 paid subscription streams or 1,500 ad-supported streams will equal one album consumption unit on the Billboard 200, against 2,500 ad-supported streams today. The new ratio takes effect on the Billboard 200 and its genre album charts dated January 16, 2027, which will reflect data from January 1-7. Billboard said the change follows its annual review, with Luminate, of the streaming revenue data that informs the methodology for the Billboard 200, the Hot 100 and other charts. YouTube's global head of music, Lyor Cohen, confirmed the return, writing 'We are returning to the Billboard charts starting in 2027. Billboard's new methodology better reflects how fans engage with music today.' YouTube's data has been absent from Billboard's charts since the charts dated January 31 this year. YouTube said in October 2025 that it had paid more than $8 billion to the music industry in the 12 months from July 2024 to June 2025, and Alphabet disclosed that YouTube Music and Premium had surpassed 150 million subscribers globally.

articles.title: Warner Music France fully acquires Délicieuse Musique, the Bordeaux label group with a 1,200-plus artist roster
articles.description: Warner Music France has acquired French independent music company Délicieuse Musique, and MBW has confirmed it now owns 100% of the share capital. The Bordeaux-based firm, founded in 2012, runs ten imprints and manages a roster of more than 1,200 artists.
articles.body: Warner Music France has acquired French independent music company Délicieuse Musique, and MBW has confirmed that WMG has acquired 100% of the share capital, though the company will continue to be run autonomously from Bordeaux. The firm's related publishing company, GLM Editions, remains independent. The deal, announced on Sunday, November 8, gives Délicieuse's labels and artists access to Warner Music Group's global resources for digital distribution, marketing, sync licensing and brand partnerships. The financial terms were not disclosed. Délicieuse's portfolio includes the labels Délicieuse Records, Nice Guys, Noire & Blanche, Egoplanet, Crosswalk and Hip Dozer, and the company, founded in 2012, represents ten imprints and manages a roster of more than 1,200 artists across multiple genres. The investment comes less than a week after WMG acquired Zebralution Music, a distributor for independent record labels in Germany and across Europe, bringing the Berlin-based business back under Warner ownership. France, the world's sixth-largest recorded music market, generated total recorded music revenues of €1.071 billion in 2025, and SNEP reported the market grew 3.5% year-on-year to €449 million in the first half of 2026.

articles.title: Universal Music Group generated €3.394 billion in Q3, up 11.7% year-on-year
articles.description: Universal Music Group's revenues for the three months to the end of September 2026 rose 11.7% year-on-year at constant currency to €3.394 billion ($3.90 billion) across recorded music, publishing and more, according to results published on October 29. MBW founder Tim Ingham unpacked five takeaways, from 'supercharged' artist-centric royalties to Downtown's margins and more cost cuts.
articles.body: Universal Music Group generated revenues of €3.394 billion across all of its divisions, including recorded music, publishing and more, in the third quarter of 2026, up 11.7% year-on-year at constant currency, according to results published on October 29. In dollar terms the total was $3.90 billion. MBW founder Tim Ingham unpacked five takeaways from the results, ranging from 'supercharged' artist-centric royalties to the margins at Downtown, the services business UMG acquired, and further cost cuts across the group. The quarter keeps UMG on a strong growth trajectory in a year when all three majors have been expanding, with Sony Music Group posting a record $3.15 billion quarter in the same period. The results underline the majors' continued growth even as the industry fights its AI copyright battles in court, with Reservoir's lawsuits against Suno and Anthropic now covering more than 2,500 songs. UMG's performance also sets the context for Warner Music Group's fiscal fourth-quarter earnings call on November 19, which will complete the majors' 2026 reporting season.

articles.title: GTA VI: The Album' full 34-track list leaks online and Rolling Stone confirms it is real
articles.description: The full 34-track soundtrack for Grand Theft Auto VI leaked online when an image of the album's vinyl tracklist spread on Reddit and X, and Rolling Stone confirmed the image is legitimate. Only 10 of the 34 tracks had been officially confirmed before the leak. The game itself launches on Thursday, November 19.
articles.body: The full tracklist for Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album has surfaced online, and it appears to be the genuine article, with Rolling Stone confirming the leaked image is legitimate. The leak began when a photo of the album's vinyl tracklist spread on Reddit and X, and it matters because Rockstar had held most of the album back: only 10 of the 34 tracks were officially confirmed before the leak. The tracklist includes new songs from Lana Del Rey, Dua Lipa and Zara Larsson, alongside Jennie, Arca, Morgan Wallen, Keith Richards, Travis Scott, SZA, Tame Impala and Playboi Carti, plus Justice with Michael McDonald. Rockstar announced the album on September 17, working with Atlantic Records, and has yet to officially confirm the full list. The album is separate from Justice's 50-song score, which is due December 11. A Miami festival on November 21 will feature Cardi B, Kodak Black and Don Toliver, among others. The game launches Thursday, November 19, for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, with preloading already under way and the game taking up 115 GB on PS5.

articles.title: Phil Collins, tears in his eyes at his Rock Hall induction, vows 'You haven't heard the last of me'
articles.description: Phil Collins, 75, was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame as a solo artist on Saturday at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, with Travis Barker delivering the induction speech and Cynthia Erivo singing a slowed-down 'In the Air Tonight' while Barker played the famous drum fill. Collins, who walked with two canes and did not perform, told the crowd: 'I'm really not as bad as it looks. I'm much better.'
articles.body: Phil Collins was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame as a solo artist on Saturday night, joining the institution for a second time after previously entering as a member of Genesis in 2010. Fellow drummer Travis Barker welcomed Collins into the Hall at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, praising him for his dual stardom as a drummer and a hit-making pop singer in the 1980s, and Cynthia Erivo sang a slowed-down, epic rendition of 'In the Air Tonight' while Barker played the song's famous drum fill. Collins walked the red carpet using two canes, accompanied by his family, including his actor daughters Lily and Joely Collins and son Nicholas Collins, and he moved slowly to the stage to accept the honour. He did not perform during the ceremony, having previously declined because he did not consider himself ready, but he addressed the room directly, telling the audience: 'I'm really not as bad as it looks. I'm much better,' and vowing: 'You haven't heard the last of me.' Health issues and knee surgeries have kept the musician off the stage since March 2022, and he has left the door open to touring again, saying 'I never say exactly never.' The 2026 ceremony was taped on November 14 and will air on ABC on December 8 and on Disney+ the following day.

articles.title: Stephen Wilson Jr. performs an acoustic 'Wonderwall' as a tribute to Oasis at the Rock Hall ceremony
articles.description: Country artist Stephen Wilson Jr. performed a solo acoustic version of Oasis's 'Wonderwall' at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame ceremony, a tribute to the band inducted in the Performer category. Rolling Stone described the interpretation as deep, raspy and noticeably different from Liam Gallagher's vocal style.
articles.body: Country artist Stephen Wilson Jr. performed a solo acoustic version of Oasis's song 'Wonderwall' at the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame ceremony, a tribute to the group inducted into the Hall of Fame for 2026 in the Performer category. The ceremony took place on November 14 at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. Rolling Stone described the interpretation as deep, raspy and noticeably different from Liam Gallagher's vocal style, noting that Wilson used a pedalboard alongside his acoustic guitar to add another sonic dimension to the minimalist setup.
